# Invoke-AACPolicyAssessment

## SYNOPSIS

Assesses Azure Policy across a tenant, management group or set of subscriptions - what is assigned, how compliant it is (overall, by subscription, assignment, policy and category), the exemptions and the managed identities' roles - and what to improve, with a Spectre.Console view, objects, and CSV, PDF and interactive HTML reports. In the spirit of AzPolicyLens (github.com/Azure/AzPolicyLens).

## SYNTAX

### Tenant (Default)

```
Invoke-AACPolicyAssessment [-Audience <string>] [-ComplianceWarningPercent <int>]
 [-ExemptionWarningDays <int>] [-CsvPath <string>] [-PdfPath <string>] [-HtmlPath <string>]
 [-Title <string>] [-PassThru] [-NoDisplay] [-NoPaging]
```

### ManagementGroup

```
Invoke-AACPolicyAssessment -ManagementGroupId <string> [-Audience <string>]
 [-ComplianceWarningPercent <int>] [-ExemptionWarningDays <int>] [-CsvPath <string>]
 [-PdfPath <string>] [-HtmlPath <string>] [-Title <string>] [-PassThru] [-NoDisplay] [-NoPaging]
```

### Subscription

```
Invoke-AACPolicyAssessment -SubscriptionId <string[]> [-Audience <string>]
 [-ComplianceWarningPercent <int>] [-ExemptionWarningDays <int>] [-CsvPath <string>]
 [-PdfPath <string>] [-HtmlPath <string>] [-Title <string>] [-PassThru] [-NoDisplay] [-NoPaging]
```

## ALIASES

This command has no aliases.

## DESCRIPTION

Read-only (Reader is enough), Azure Resource Graph only - no Az
modules. Every assignment, exemption, custom definition and
initiative, and the management group hierarchy are read tenant-wide,
so what a management group assigns to a subscription is there; the
built-in definitions that are assigned are read by ID; compliance is
read in the subscriptions in scope.

Compliance is counted as AzPolicyLens counts it: each resource once,
at its worst state (NonCompliant, then Compliant, Conflict, Exempt),
and compliance = (compliant + exempt) / all - overall, by
subscription, by management group, by assignment (and subscription),
by policy and by category. Under -ComplianceWarningPercent (80) is
Warning, under half of it Poor.

Every assigned initiative is opened up (InitiativePolicies, and the
initiative-policies CSV and HTML table): each member policy with its
effect - an effect override on the assignment included - the value
each of its parameters ends up with (from the assignment, else the
initiative or the policy's default, as noted) and its compliance.
For one row per policy and parameter, see Get-AACAssignedPolicy
-ExpandPolicySet.

The findings (each with its severity, what was found and what to do):

```text
  Assignments  definitions assigned directly (not in an initiative),
               DoNotEnforce, a definition that can't be found,
               below the compliance threshold, deprecated or preview
               policies assigned, excluded scopes that don't exist,
               the same definition assigned twice on a scope path,
               Deny with no non-compliance message
  Identity     DeployIfNotExists and Modify assignments with no
               managed identity, or one missing the roles their
               policies list
  Exemptions   expired, expiring within -ExemptionWarningDays (30),
               never expiring, for an assignment that is gone
  Definitions  unassigned custom definitions and initiatives, unused
               policy definition groups, the same control under
               different group names, no category in the metadata
  Compliance   subscriptions below the threshold
```

-Audience Platform (the default; AzPolicyLens's detailed wiki) is for
the team that runs Azure Policy: everything, with hidden- metadata and
tags. Application (its basic wiki) is for an application team: their
assignments, compliance and exemptions, without the unassigned
definitions, metadata hygiene or hidden- metadata.

What you get depends on where the command runs:

```text
  at the prompt    tiles, compliance by subscription and category,
                   the assignments least compliant first, the
                   exemptions that need attention and the High and
                   Medium findings, a page at a time
  piped onward     the AAC.PolicyAssignmentReport objects, each with
                   its Compliance, PolicyStates,
                   InitiativePolicies and Findings
  -PassThru        the view and the objects
  -NoDisplay       the objects only
```

-CsvPath (a folder) writes a CSV per table. -HtmlPath writes an
interactive report - the management group hierarchy as a tree with
each level's compliance, then every table; -PdfPath a PDF.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1

```powershell
Connect-AAC
Invoke-AACPolicyAssessment
```

Azure Policy across every subscription and management group the account can see.

### Example 2

```powershell
Invoke-AACPolicyAssessment -ManagementGroupId 'mg-landingzones' -HtmlPath .\out\Policy.html -PdfPath .\out\Policy.pdf -CsvPath .\out\policy
A landing zone's policy, with every report.
```

### Example 3

```powershell
Invoke-AACPolicyAssessment -SubscriptionId 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 -Audience Application -HtmlPath .\Policy.html
```

An application team's report: the policies on their subscription, how compliant it is, and their exemptions.

### Example 4

```powershell
Invoke-AACPolicyAssessment -NoDisplay | Where-Object { $_.Rating -ne 'Good' } | Select-Object Assignment, Scope, CompliancePercent, NonCompliant
```

The assignments under the compliance threshold.

### Example 5

```powershell
(Invoke-AACPolicyAssessment -NoDisplay | Where-Object Assignment -Like '*PostgreSQL*').InitiativePolicies | Format-Table Policy, Effect, Parameters, CompliancePercent
```

The policies inside an initiative assignment: effect, parameter values and compliance.

# Invoke-AACPSRule

## SYNOPSIS

Checks your live Azure estate with PSRule for Azure - its Azure Well-Architected Framework rules, the module's own rules and your custom rules - with a console view, objects, and CSV, PDF and interactive HTML reports.

## SYNTAX

### __AllParameterSets

```
Invoke-AACPSRule [[-SubscriptionId] <string[]>] [[-ResourceType] <string[]>] [[-Rule] <string[]>]
 [[-ExcludeRule] <string[]>] [[-Baseline] <string>] [[-Configuration] <hashtable>]
 [[-RulePath] <string[]>] [[-CsvPath] <string>] [[-PdfPath] <string>] [[-HtmlPath] <string>]
 [[-Title] <string>] [-NoExpand] [-FailedOnly] [-PassThru] [-NoDisplay] [-NoPaging]
```

## ALIASES

This command has no aliases.

## DESCRIPTION

Runs PSRule for Azure (the PSRule.Rules.Azure module, 500+ rules)
against every resource, resource group and subscription the
signed-in account can see, or those in -SubscriptionId. No Az modules:
the data PSRule needs - what Export-AzRuleData would export - is read
with the Connect-AAC sign-in, from Azure Resource Graph plus the child
settings PSRule's rules look at (storage blob services, SQL auditing,
Key Vault diagnostic settings, App Service config, API Management
APIs and policies, ...). Reader on the subscriptions is enough.

The rules that run:

```text
  PSRule for Azure    every rule of the installed PSRule.Rules.Azure
                      (-Baseline picks one of its baselines)
  Azure.Admin.Console the module's own AAC.* rules (PSRule\Rules):
                      required tags on resources and resource
                      groups and allowed tag values - the tags
                      named in -Configuration or in
                      Get-AACTagDefault (PSRule\Rules\AAC.Tags.Rule.ps1);
                      with none named they check nothing, and the
                      view says so - and naming conventions (on by default: the
                      Cloud Adoption Framework abbreviations, or
                      AAC_NAMING_PATTERNS)
  custom              your own PSRule rule files (*.Rule.ps1,
                      *.Rule.yaml, *.Rule.jsonc) from -RulePath
```

-Rule runs only the rules named, and -ExcludeRule leaves rules out;
both take names or wildcards ('Azure.Storage.\*', 'AAC.\*').
-Configuration passes settings to all of them: PSRule for Azure's
AZURE_\* options and the AAC_\* settings.

What you get depends on where the command runs:

```text
  at the prompt    a Spectre.Console view: tiles (objects, rules,
                   passed, failed, pass rate), failures by pillar,
                   then a table per pillar with each failing rule,
                   the resources it failed on and why - a page at a
                   time (-NoPaging turns that off)
  piped onward     the AAC.PSRuleResult objects, with no view
  -PassThru        the view and the objects
  -NoDisplay       the objects only
```

Exports:

```text
  -CsvPath    one row per rule and resource (-FailedOnly: failures
              only)
  -PdfPath    a landscape A4 report: summary and verdict, results
              by pillar, the failed rules, then every failing
              resource per rule with the rule's recommendation and
              documentation link
  -HtmlPath   a self-contained, interactive HTML report: clickable
              tiles and charts, and every result in one table that
              opens on the failures, grouped by rule, with search,
              filters, portal and documentation links and a CSV
              download
```

When any of them is given, the console shows only the progress and
the files written; add -PassThru for the objects too.

PSRule runs in a pwsh process of its own, so its YamlDotNet.dll
never meets the different versions platyPS, powershell-yaml or Az.Aks
may have loaded in this session. A rule that can't evaluate a
resource is reported for that resource ("could not evaluate");
every other rule still runs. Settings Reader can't read are listed
as warnings, as rules using them may be wrong for those resources.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1

```powershell
Connect-AAC
Invoke-AACPSRule
```

Checks every resource you can see and shows what failed.

### Example 2

```powershell
Invoke-AACPSRule -SubscriptionId '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000' -HtmlPath .\out\PSRule.html
```

One subscription, as an interactive HTML report.

### Example 3

```powershell
Invoke-AACPSRule -CsvPath .\out\PSRule.csv -PdfPath .\out\PSRule.pdf -FailedOnly
```

The failures as a CSV file and a PDF report.

### Example 4

```powershell
Invoke-AACPSRule -Rule 'Azure.Storage.*', 'Azure.KeyVault.*' -ExcludeRule 'Azure.Storage.Name'
```

Only the storage and Key Vault rules, without the storage naming rule.

### Example 5

```powershell
Invoke-AACPSRule -Baseline 'Azure.Pillar.Security'
```

Only PSRule for Azure's security pillar baseline.

### Example 6

```powershell
Invoke-AACPSRule -Configuration @{ AAC_REQUIRED_TAGS = @('Owner', 'CostCenter'); AAC_ALLOWED_TAG_VALUES = @{ Environment = @('prod', 'test', 'dev') }; AZURE_RESOURCE_ALLOWED_LOCATIONS = @('uksouth', 'ukwest') }
```

Adds the module's tag rules and PSRule for Azure's allowed regions.

### Example 7

```powershell
Invoke-AACPSRule -Rule 'AAC.Resource.Naming'
```

Checks names against the Cloud Adoption Framework abbreviations, reading only the types it checks.

### Example 8

```powershell
Invoke-AACPSRule -RulePath .\MyRules -ExcludeRule 'AAC.*'
```

Runs your own rules from .\MyRules with PSRule for Azure's, without the module's.

### Example 9

```powershell
Invoke-AACPSRule -FailedOnly | Group-Object RuleName | Sort-Object Count -Descending | Select-Object -First 10 Count, Name
```

The ten rules that fail most.

# Invoke-AACSentinelAssessment

## SYNOPSIS

Assesses Microsoft Sentinel on a Log Analytics workspace: analytics rules and MITRE ATT&CK coverage, rule templates, data connectors, tables and ingestion, health failures, incidents, automation rules and recommendations - with a Spectre.Console view, an object, and CSV and interactive HTML and PDF reports.

## SYNTAX

### __AllParameterSets

```
Invoke-AACSentinelAssessment [-WorkspaceId] <string> [-SubscriptionId <string[]>] [-Days <int>]
 [-Section <string[]>] [-IncludeEmptyTable] [-CsvPath <string>] [-HtmlPath <string>]
 [-PdfPath <string>] [-Title <string>] [-PassThru] [-NoDisplay] [-NoPaging]
```

## ALIASES

This command has no aliases.

## DESCRIPTION

Reads one workspace - read-only, nothing is changed - from:

```text
  Azure Resource Manager   whether Sentinel is enabled, its analytics
                           rules and templates, data connectors,
                           incidents and automation rules, and the
                           workspace's tables (plan, retention)
  the workspace itself     KQL: Usage (size and last record per table),
                           _SentinelHealth (failures per resource) and
                           SecurityIncident (when incidents closed)
```

-WorkspaceId is the workspace ID (its customerId GUID, as the portal
shows it), the full resource ID, or the workspace's name.

What comes back:

```text
  AnalyticsRules    every rule: kind, severity, enabled, tactics,
                    frequency, query, its health failures and
                    incidents. Failing rules first.
  TacticCoverage    how many enabled rules declare each MITRE ATT&CK
                    Enterprise tactic
  RuleTemplates     every template the API lists (built-in and from
                    installed solutions): the data it needs, whether
                    that data is arriving and whether a rule uses it.
                    Candidates - data arriving, no rule yet - first.
  Incidents         every incident created in the last -Days: severity,
                    status, owner, classification, hours to close.
                    These hold people's names and email addresses, and
                    so do the reports.
  AutomationRules   every automation rule, in the order they run:
                    state, triggers, actions, expiry
  DataConnectors    every connector the API lists: kind, state, data
                    types. A source can send data without being listed
                    here, so Tables is what shows what really arrives.
  Tables            billable and free GB over -Days, share of billable
                    data, daily average, plan, retention, last record.
                    Tables with no data are left out unless custom, or
                    with -IncludeEmptyTable.
  HealthFailures    what _SentinelHealth reports as failed: resource,
                    operation, count, last failure and reason
  Recommendations   Sentinel not enabled, enabled rules failing, tables
                    that stopped receiving data, health monitoring off,
                    connector or automation failures, billable tables
                    no enabled rule reads, templates to enable, MITRE
                    ATT&CK gaps, incidents with no owner or slow to
                    close, noisy rules, expired or disabled automation,
                    rules with a newer template - by severity, with
                    what to do
```

-Section limits the reading to some of: AnalyticsRules, RuleTemplates,
DataConnectors, Tables, Health, Incidents, AutomationRules,
Recommendations.

Needs Microsoft Sentinel Reader and Log Analytics Reader on the
workspace. What can't be read is reported, and the rest carries on.

What you get depends on where the command runs:

```text
  at the prompt    tiles, then each section - a page at a time
  piped onward     the assessment object, with no view
  -PassThru        the view and the object
  -NoDisplay       the object only
```

-CsvPath writes the analytics rules (one row each). -HtmlPath writes a
tabbed interactive report - a Summary (headline, tiles, charts), then
a tab per section - every table searchable, filterable and
downloadable as CSV. -PdfPath writes the same as a PDF, each section a
bookmarked heading.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1

```powershell
Connect-AAC
Invoke-AACSentinelAssessment -WorkspaceId 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
```

The whole assessment of one workspace, by its workspace ID.

### Example 2

```powershell
Invoke-AACSentinelAssessment -WorkspaceId 'law-contoso-sentinel' -Days 7 -Section Tables, Health
```

Ingestion and health failures over the last 7 days.

### Example 3

```powershell

A tabbed HTML report and a PDF, and the analytics rules as CSV.
```

### Example 4

```powershell
(Invoke-AACSentinelAssessment -WorkspaceId 'law-contoso-sentinel' -Section RuleTemplates -NoDisplay).RuleTemplates | Where-Object Candidate
```

The templates worth enabling: their data is arriving and no rule uses them.

### Example 5

```powershell
(Invoke-AACSentinelAssessment -WorkspaceId 'law-contoso-sentinel' -Section AnalyticsRules -NoDisplay).AnalyticsRules | Where-Object Enabled -EQ $false
```

The analytics rules that are turned off.

### Example 6

```powershell
(Invoke-AACSentinelAssessment -WorkspaceId 'law-contoso-sentinel' -NoDisplay).Recommendations | Where-Object Severity -EQ 'High'
```

The high-severity recommendations.

# Invoke-AACServiceBusAssessment

## SYNOPSIS

Assesses Azure Service Bus namespaces across subscriptions - health, capacity, every queue, topic and subscription's messages (active, dead-lettered, scheduled), security, resilience and cost - as a heat map, findings, a Spectre.Console view, objects, and CSV, PDF and interactive HTML reports.

## SYNTAX

### __AllParameterSets

```
Invoke-AACServiceBusAssessment [[-SubscriptionId] <string[]>] [[-ManagementGroupId] <string[]>]
 [[-ResourceGroupName] <string[]>] [[-Name] <string[]>] [[-TimeRange] <string>] [[-View] <string>]
 [[-ThrottleLimit] <int>] [[-CsvPath] <string>] [[-HtmlPath] <string>] [[-PdfPath] <string>]
 [[-Title] <string>] [-PassThru] [-NoDisplay] [-NoPaging]
```

## ALIASES

This command has no aliases.

## DESCRIPTION

Read-only (Reader is enough):

```text
  Resource Graph    the namespaces: tier, messaging units, TLS, local
                    (SAS) authentication, public network access, zone
                    redundancy, private endpoints, encryption
  Resource Manager  each namespace's queues, topics and their
                    subscriptions (message counts and sizes as they
                    are now), network rules, SAS rules, geo-disaster
                    recovery alias, and where its logs go
  metrics           over -TimeRange: IncomingRequests,
                    SuccessfulRequests, ServerErrors, UserErrors,
                    ThrottledRequests, IncomingMessages,
                    OutgoingMessages - and for Premium,
                    NamespaceCpuUsage and NamespaceMemoryUsage
```

Findings (High, Medium, Low):

```text
  health      throttled requests, server errors, many client errors
              (lost locks, missing entities)
  capacity    Premium CPU or memory close to the messaging units'
              limit
  messages    dead-lettered and transfer dead-lettered messages,
              entities filling up (sends fail at 100%), entities not
              active, active backlogs, topics with no subscription,
              expired messages dropped instead of dead-lettered
  security    TLS below 1.2, SAS keys allowed, more than one
              namespace-wide Manage key, open to every network, no
              logs to Log Analytics
  resilience  Premium not zone redundant, no geo-disaster recovery,
              Basic tier
  cost        more messaging units than needed, no requests in the
              period, queues and topics unused for 30 days
```

The heat map scores each namespace 0-100 for health, capacity,
messages, security, resilience and cost - the 40 worst at the prompt
and in the reports; clicking a cell in the HTML lists its findings.

-View sets what is returned (piped onward, -PassThru, -NoDisplay) and
written to -CsvPath: Namespace (default), Entity or Finding.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1

```powershell
Connect-AAC
Invoke-AACServiceBusAssessment
```

Every namespace's health, messages, posture and findings over the last day.

### Example 2

```powershell
Invoke-AACServiceBusAssessment -View Entity -NoDisplay | Where-Object DeadLetters | Sort-Object -Property DeadLetters -Descending
```

The queues and subscriptions with dead-lettered messages, the most first.

### Example 3

```powershell
Invoke-AACServiceBusAssessment -ResourceGroupName 'rg-integration' -TimeRange 7d -HtmlPath .\out\ServiceBus.html -PdfPath .\out\ServiceBus.pdf
A week of a workload's namespaces, as reports.
```

### Example 4

```powershell
Invoke-AACServiceBusAssessment -View Finding -NoDisplay | Where-Object Signal -EQ 'Security'
```

The security findings, to fix.

# Invoke-AACStorageAccountAssessment

## SYNOPSIS

Assesses storage accounts across subscriptions - what Azure Monitor's Storage accounts workbook shows (transactions, latency, errors by response type, capacity by service) plus availability, throttling, security posture, data protection and cost - as a heat map, findings, a Spectre.Console view, objects, and CSV, PDF and interactive HTML reports.

## SYNTAX

### __AllParameterSets

```
Invoke-AACStorageAccountAssessment [[-SubscriptionId] <string[]>] [[-ManagementGroupId] <string[]>]
 [[-ResourceGroupName] <string[]>] [[-Name] <string[]>] [[-TimeRange] <string>] [[-View] <string>]
 [[-ThrottleLimit] <int>] [[-CsvPath] <string>] [[-HtmlPath] <string>] [[-PdfPath] <string>]
 [[-Title] <string>] [-PassThru] [-NoDisplay] [-NoPaging]
```

## ALIASES

This command has no aliases.

## DESCRIPTION

Read-only (Reader is enough):

```text
  Resource Graph   the accounts, the Defender for Storage plan and its
                   alerts
  metrics          per account over -TimeRange - the workbook's
                   Overview tab: Transactions, SuccessE2ELatency,
                   SuccessServerLatency, Transactions by ResponseType,
                   plus Availability, Ingress and Egress
  capacity         the workbook's Capacity tab, the latest value:
                   UsedCapacity, BlobCapacity (with BlobCount and
                   ContainerCount), FileCapacity (and FileShareCount),
                   QueueCapacity and TableCapacity - capacity is
                   reported hourly to daily, so it is always read over
                   at least the last two days
  settings         blob and container soft delete, versioning, change
                   feed, point-in-time restore, file share soft
                   delete, lifecycle rules and where the blob logs go
```

Response types are grouped: Success, Throttling (ClientThrottling\*,
ServerBusy\*), Server (ServerTimeout, ServerOther), Authorization
(Authorization, Authentication), Network (Network, ClientTimeout) and
Client (ClientOther - mostly 404 and 409, often normal: they don't
count as errors).

Findings (High, Medium, Low):

```text
  health      availability under 99.9%, throttling, server errors,
              authorization failures, network errors, slow server
              responses, time lost between client and service
  security    HTTP allowed, TLS below 1.2, anonymous blob access, open
              to every network, shared key access, keys not rotated
              in 90 days, no key or SAS expiration policy, cross-
              tenant replication, no blob logs, Defender off or
              alerting
  protection  LRS only, blob, container and file share soft delete
              off (or under 7 days), versioning off
  cost        general-purpose v1 or legacy Blob storage accounts, no
              lifecycle rules, idle accounts, hot tier with little
              activity
```

The heat map scores each account 0-100 for availability, errors,
throttling, latency, security, protection and cost - the 40 worst at
the prompt and in the reports; clicking a cell in the HTML lists its
findings. The reports' tabs follow the workbook - Overview and
Capacity - then Security & protection and Findings.

-View sets what is returned (piped onward, -PassThru, -NoDisplay) and
written to -CsvPath: Account (default) or Finding.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1

```powershell
Connect-AAC
Invoke-AACStorageAccountAssessment
```

Every storage account's health, capacity, posture and findings over the last day.

### Example 2

```powershell
Invoke-AACStorageAccountAssessment -ResourceGroupName 'rg-data' -TimeRange 7d -HtmlPath .\out\Storage.html -PdfPath .\out\Storage.pdf
A week of a workload's storage accounts, as reports.
```

### Example 3

```powershell
Invoke-AACStorageAccountAssessment -View Finding -NoDisplay | Where-Object Signal -EQ 'Security'
```

The security findings, to fix.

### Example 4

```powershell
Invoke-AACStorageAccountAssessment -NoDisplay | Sort-Object -Property UsedGB -Descending | Select-Object -First 10 -Property Account, UsedGB, BlobGB, FileGB, AccessTier, LifecycleRules
```

The ten biggest accounts, and whether lifecycle rules keep their cost down.

# Invoke-AACTenantAssessment

## SYNOPSIS

Assesses an Azure tenant end to end - the organization, an inventory of every resource type with its key settings and policy compliance, Azure Policy, the Well-Architected Framework, PSRule for Azure, Advisor, retirements, Defender for Cloud, FinOps and cost, outages and quotas - as CSV files, an interactive HTML report, a PDF and interactive diagrams, with a live Spectre.Console progress display.

## SYNTAX

### __AllParameterSets

```
Invoke-AACTenantAssessment [[-TenantId] <string>] [[-ManagementGroupId] <string[]>]
 [[-SubscriptionId] <string[]>] [[-ResourceGroupName] <string[]>] [[-TagKey] <string>]
 [[-TagValue] <string>] [[-Category] <string[]>] [[-PSRuleBaseline] <string>]
 [[-CostTag] <string[]>] [[-ActivityDays] <int>] [[-ExpiryDays] <int>] [[-OwnerTag] <string[]>]
 [[-ProductionPattern] <string>] [[-HtmlPath] <string>] [[-PdfPath] <string>] [[-CsvPath] <string>]
 [[-DiagramPath] <string>] [[-StorageAccount] <string>] [[-StorageContainer] <string>]
 [[-Title] <string>] [-IncludeTag] [-SecurityCenter] [-SkipAdvisor] [-SkipPolicy] [-PSRule]
 [-SkipWaf] [-IncludeCost] [-QuotaUsage] [-Full] [-SkipIdentity] [-SkipKeyVault] [-SkipApi]
 [-SkipVMDetail] [-DiagramFullEnvironment] [-Automation] [-PassThru] [-NoDisplay] [-NoPaging]
```

## ALIASES

This command has no aliases.

## DESCRIPTION

The module's take on Azure Resource Inventory (ARI), and the one
command to run first in a tenant you need to understand: it reads
the tenant (or the subscriptions, management groups, resource
groups or tag you name) and writes the reports you choose.
Read-only; Reader is enough (Security Reader for Defender, Cost
Management Reader for cost); no Az modules, no Excel. -Full turns on
everything that is off by default.

The focused assessments go deeper into one service or discipline -
Invoke-AACWafAssessment (a workload's review, with the team's
answers and the trend), Invoke-AACPolicyAssessment,
Invoke-AACDefenderAssessment, Invoke-AACGovernanceAssessment and the
service ones (AKS, Cosmos DB, Function Apps, Log Analytics, Service
Bus, storage, virtual networks).

What it reads, in phases - each a line of the progress display:

```text
  1. Scope        the subscriptions (with their management groups) in
                  scope, and the tenant's management groups
  2. Estate       every resource and resource group, the resource
                  types present; Advisor recommendations (and
                  retirements, always); Defender for Cloud
                  (-SecurityCenter); Azure Policy compliance - by
                  policy, resource group and resource (unless
                  -SkipPolicy); support tickets
  3. Inventory    a sheet per resource type present - ~95 types, in
                  the categories Compute, Hybrid, Containers,
                  Databases, Analytics, AI, Integration, IoT,
                  Management, Monitoring, Networking, Security,
                  Storage and Web - each with the settings that
                  matter for it (a VM's size, power state, OS, disks,
                  IP, network and security settings; a storage
                  account's TLS, public access, shared keys and
                  firewall; ...), as Resource Graph projections
  4. Azure APIs   per subscription: the Advisor score, reservation
                  recommendations, the budgets, the last 6 months'
                  outages (Resource Health service issues), compute
                  quotas (-QuotaUsage), and VM sizes' vCPUs and
                  memory (unless -SkipVMDetail); -SkipApi skips them
                  all
  5. Well-Architected  the checks of Invoke-AACWafAssessment across
                  the five pillars - Reliability, Security, Cost
                  Optimization, Operational Excellence, Performance
                  Efficiency - scored by pillar, design principle
                  and check (unless -SkipWaf)
  6. Cost         each resource's cost, this month and last
                  (-IncludeCost, Cost Management)
  7. PSRule       PSRule for Azure's rules on the resources (-PSRule)
  8. Governance   the policy assignments in force and every policy
                  they apply (unless -SkipPolicy), FinOps, and one
                  list of recommendations
  9. Reports      the reports asked for (-HtmlPath, -PdfPath,
                  -CsvPath, -DiagramPath), then an upload to a blob
                  container (-StorageAccount)
```

Every inventory sheet (and All resources) adds, after its own
columns: Retirement (an Advisor retirement notice for the
resource), Advisor (its number of recommendations), its policy
compliance (Policy - Non-compliant, Compliant, Exempt or Not
evaluated; Non-compliant policies; Failing policies, by name), WAF
gaps (the Well-Architected checks it fails), PSRule failures (with
-PSRule), its cost with -IncludeCost, and its tags with -IncludeTag.
The overview sheets: Subscriptions, Resource groups, Resource types,
All resources; then Advisor recommendations, Advisor score,
Retirements, Security recommendations, Secure score, Policy
compliance, Outages, Quotas, Support tickets and Reservation
recommendations. Then:

```text
  Well-Architected   WAF pillars (score and maturity), WAF design
                     principles, WAF checks and WAF findings (each
                     failed check on each resource, with what to do)
  FinOps             Savings opportunities (by lever: Waste -
                     unattached disks, unused public IPs, VMs
                     stopped but billed, empty plans, old snapshots;
                     Rightsizing and Rate - Advisor's cost
                     recommendations, reservations, savings plans;
                     Licensing - Azure Hybrid Benefit; Modernise -
                     old VM generations - each with its estimated
                     annual saving), Cost allocation (the resources
                     with a cost-allocation tag, -CostTag, and the
                     cost of those without), Budgets (spent and
                     forecast against each budget, the alerts, the
                     subscriptions with none) and, with
                     -IncludeCost, Cost by service, Cost by
                     resource group and Top cost resources (this
                     month projected against last month)
```

and the governance sheets:

```text
  Policy compliance  Compliance by initiative, by resource group and
                     by standard (the controls of CIS, NIST, ISO
                     27001, the Microsoft cloud security benchmark
                     ... initiatives), and each non-compliant
                     resource with why and how to fix it
  Policy inventory   Policy assignments, and every policy in force
                     with its effect, resource types, controls and
                     status (Failed, Passed, Manual review, Exempt,
                     Not evaluated, Disabled)
  PSRule results     PSRule rules (checked, passed, failed, with
                     their documentation) and the failed resources
                     (-PSRule)
  Recommendations    Resource recommendations: Advisor, Defender,
                     retirements, unattached and empty resources,
                     policy non-compliance, PSRule, the
                     Well-Architected findings and FinOps (budgets,
                     cost allocation) in one list, each with a
                     severity, category and what to do
```

The reports - each written only where its own parameter says, none
by default:

```text
  -HtmlPath     a tabbed workbook: an Executive summary (tiles - the
            Well-Architected score, the estimated savings, cost-tag
            coverage ... - charts - a click filters the table behind
            them - and the tenant tree), then Policy compliance,
            Policy inventory, Well-Architected, PSRule results,
            Resource recommendations, FinOps, Resources, Inventory,
            Advisor, Security and Health; every table
            searchable, filterable, groupable, with each row's
            details a click away, and downloadable as CSV
  -PdfPath      the summary, then each category with its sheets' key
                columns (bookmarked)
  -CsvPath      a folder: a CSV file per sheet
  -DiagramPath  a folder: TenantAssessment-Network.html, the network
                topology - virtual networks, subnets, peerings,
                gateways, firewalls, load balancers, private
                endpoints, NSGs and routes (-DiagramFullEnvironment:
                every resource and how they connect);
                TenantAssessment-Organization.html, management
                groups > subscriptions > resource groups;
                TenantAssessment-Resources.html, each subscription
                with its resource types and counts. Interactive:
                pan, zoom, search, details on click, PNG and SVG
                export.
```

Without any of them the run shows its summary and returns the
assessment (-PassThru, -NoDisplay): every sheet is in its Sheets.

Sign-in: the Connect-AAC session. -TenantId signs in to that tenant
first (in the browser) when the session is for another one. In
Azure Automation, -Automation signs in with the account's managed
identity (Connect-AAC -Identity) if no session is there yet, and
writes plain progress lines for the job log. -StorageAccount and
-StorageContainer upload the reports written to blob storage, under
TenantAssessment/\<date\>/ (Storage Blob Data Contributor needed);
with no report path given, every report is written to a temporary
folder for the upload.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1

```powershell
Connect-AAC
Invoke-AACTenantAssessment -HtmlPath .\Tenant.html -PdfPath .\Tenant.pdf
```

The whole tenant (everything the account can see), as an HTML and a PDF report.

### Example 2

```powershell
Invoke-AACTenantAssessment -HtmlPath C:\Reports\Tenant.html -CsvPath C:\Reports\csv -DiagramPath C:\Reports\diagrams
```

The HTML report, a CSV file per sheet and the diagrams, each where you say.

### Example 3

```powershell
Invoke-AACTenantAssessment -TenantId 'contoso.onmicrosoft.com' -Full
```

Another tenant, with everything: Defender for Cloud, cost, tags, PSRule for Azure and quotas.

### Example 4

```powershell
Invoke-AACTenantAssessment -SecurityCenter -IncludeTag -IncludeCost -CostTag 'CostCenter', 'Department'
```

Defender for Cloud, tags and cost, with the organisation's own cost-allocation tags.

### Example 5

```powershell
(Invoke-AACTenantAssessment -IncludeCost -NoDisplay).Sheets['Savings opportunities'] | Sort-Object 'Est. annual savings' -Descending | Select-Object -First 10
```

The ten biggest savings.

### Example 6

```powershell
(Invoke-AACTenantAssessment -NoDisplay).Sheets['All resources'] | Where-Object Policy -EQ 'Non-compliant' | Select-Object Name, Type, 'Failing policies'
```

Each non-compliant resource and the policies it fails.

### Example 7

```powershell
Invoke-AACTenantAssessment -ManagementGroupId 'mg-landingzones' -HtmlPath .\LandingZones.html -DiagramPath .\diagrams
A management group's subscriptions: the HTML report and the diagrams.
```

### Example 8

```powershell
Invoke-AACTenantAssessment -SubscriptionId 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 -TagKey 'Environment' -TagValue 'Production' -Category Compute, Networking
```

Production's compute and network resources in one subscription.

### Example 9

```powershell
Invoke-AACTenantAssessment -Automation -StorageAccount 'stcontosoreports' -StorageContainer 'assessments'
```

In an Azure Automation runbook: managed identity sign-in, and every report uploaded to blob storage.

### Example 10

```powershell
(Invoke-AACTenantAssessment -NoDisplay).Sheets['Virtual machines'] | Where-Object 'Power state' -NE 'VM running'
```

The VMs that aren't running.

# Invoke-AACVirtualNetworkAssessment

## SYNOPSIS

Assesses virtual networks: address space and available IPs, every subnet, peerings, NSGs and application security groups, DNS, DDoS, flow logs, outbound access and gateways - with findings and what to do, a Spectre.Console view, objects, and CSV, PDF and interactive HTML reports.

## SYNTAX

### __AllParameterSets

```
Invoke-AACVirtualNetworkAssessment [[-SubscriptionId] <string[]>] [[-ManagementGroupId] <string[]>]
 [[-ResourceGroupName] <string[]>] [[-Name] <string[]>] [[-CsvPath] <string>] [[-PdfPath] <string>]
 [[-HtmlPath] <string>] [[-Title] <string>] [-PassThru] [-NoDisplay] [-NoPaging]
```

## ALIASES

This command has no aliases.

## DESCRIPTION

Reads, with Azure Resource Graph - read-only, Reader is enough, no Az
modules - the virtual networks and everything in or around them:
network interfaces, route tables, NAT gateways, network security
groups, application security groups, public IPs, private endpoints,
private DNS zone links, DNS resolvers, VPN and ExpressRoute gateways,
Azure Firewalls, Bastion hosts and Network Watcher flow logs.
Without parameters it assesses every virtual network the account can
see; -SubscriptionId, -ManagementGroupId, -ResourceGroupName and
-Name narrow it.

For each virtual network:

```text
  Metadata      name, role (hub, spoke, peered, standalone), location,
                resource group, subscription, tags, provisioning
                state, flow timeout, BGP community
  Address space its prefixes; total IPs, IPs in subnets, unallocated
                IPs; usable (Azure keeps 5 per subnet), used and
                available IPs; the free CIDR blocks a new subnet can
                take; overlaps with any other network you can see
  Subnets       prefix, usable / used / available IPs and % used,
                purpose (gateway, firewall, Bastion, Route Server,
                delegated, private endpoints, workloads), NSG, route
                table and its default route, BGP propagation, NAT
                gateway, the outbound path (NAT gateway, firewall or
                NVA, forced tunnelling, public IPs, private subnet,
                default outbound access), service endpoints and
                policies, delegations, private endpoints and their
                network policies, NICs, VMs, NICs with public IPs or
                IP forwarding, flow logs
  Peerings      state, sync, remote network / subscription / region,
                global, the allow* flags, gateway transit, remote
                address space, subnet peering, reverse peering
  Security      DNS servers and private DNS zone links, DDoS
                protection, virtual network encryption, flow logs,
                Firewall and Bastion, private endpoints, ASGs (who
                is in each, which rules name it) - and the NSGs on
                its subnets, assessed rule by rule as
                Get-AACNetworkSecurityGroup does
```

Findings, each with a severity, the network and item, and what to do:

```text
  High    a full subnet (or 95% used); a peering not Connected; an NSG
          or a 0.0.0.0/0 route on GatewaySubnet; Bastion, Firewall or
          Route Server subnets too small; an NSG rule open to the
          internet on a management or database port
  Medium  a subnet 80% used; a peering out of sync; a subnet with
          workloads and no NSG; VMs with public IPs; default outbound
          access (being retired); public IPs without DDoS Network
          Protection; no virtual network flow logs; private endpoints
          whose privatelink zone isn't linked; private endpoint
          connections not approved; a Basic VPN gateway; a
          GatewaySubnet under /27
  Low     oversized or empty subnets; no free address space;
          overlapping address spaces; encryption off; a single DNS
          server; private endpoint network policies off; IP
          forwarding with no route to it; empty or unused ASGs;
          gateways that aren't zone-redundant
  Info    global peering (charged per GB); a remote network you
          can't read; no Bastion where VMs have public IPs
```

What you get depends on where the command runs:

```text
  at the prompt    tiles, the networks with their IP capacity and
                   risk, the High and Medium findings, and - for up
                   to three networks - each in detail with its
                   subnets, peerings and free ranges, a page at a time
  piped onward     the AAC.VirtualNetwork objects (each with its
                   Subnets, Peerings, FreeRangeList,
                   PrivateEndpointList and Findings), with no view
  -PassThru        the view and the objects
  -NoDisplay       the objects only
```

-CsvPath writes every subnet to CSV. -HtmlPath writes an interactive
report - tiles, charts and tables of networks, subnets, peerings,
free ranges, findings, private endpoints, ASGs and NSG rules, each
collapsible and downloadable as CSV. -PdfPath writes a PDF with a
section per network. With any of them, the console shows only the
progress and the files written.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1

```powershell
Connect-AAC
Invoke-AACVirtualNetworkAssessment
```

Every virtual network the account can see, assessed.

### Example 2

```powershell
Invoke-AACVirtualNetworkAssessment -SubscriptionId 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 -Name 'vnet-hub-*', 'vnet-spoke-app'
```

Some networks in detail: subnets, peerings, free ranges and findings.

### Example 3

```powershell
Invoke-AACVirtualNetworkAssessment -ManagementGroupId 'mg-landingzones' -HtmlPath .\out\VNet.html -PdfPath .\out\VNet.pdf -CsvPath .\out\Subnets.csv
A landing zone's networks as an interactive HTML report, a PDF and a CSV of every subnet.
```

### Example 4

```powershell
(Invoke-AACVirtualNetworkAssessment -NoDisplay).Subnets | Where-Object UsedPercent -GE 80 | Sort-Object UsedPercent -Descending
```

The subnets running out of IPs.

### Example 5

```powershell
Invoke-AACVirtualNetworkAssessment -Name 'vnet-spoke-app' -NoDisplay | Select-Object -ExpandProperty FreeRangeList
```

Where a new subnet fits.

# Invoke-AACWafAssessment

## SYNOPSIS

Assesses the estate against the Azure Well-Architected Framework's five pillars - Reliability, Security, Cost Optimization, Operational Excellence and Performance Efficiency - scored by pillar, design principle and check, with workbook-style heat maps by subscription, resource group or resource type, findings and what to do, a Spectre.Console view, objects, and CSV, PDF and interactive HTML reports.

## SYNTAX

### __AllParameterSets

```
Invoke-AACWafAssessment [[-SubscriptionId] <string[]>] [[-ManagementGroupId] <string[]>]
 [[-ResourceGroupName] <string[]>] [[-Pillar] <string[]>] [[-HeatMapBy] <string>]
 [[-ExcludeCheck] <string[]>] [[-AttestationPath] <string>] [[-HistoryPath] <string>]
 [[-CostTag] <string[]>] [[-OwnerTag] <string[]>] [[-CsvPath] <string>] [[-HtmlPath] <string>]
 [[-PdfPath] <string>] [[-Title] <string>] [-NoAdvisor] [-NoDefender] [-KeepDuplicates] [-PassThru]
 [-NoDisplay] [-NoPaging]
```

## ALIASES

This command has no aliases.

## DESCRIPTION

Read-only, with one batch of Azure Resource Graph queries - Reader is
enough, no Az modules. Every check is evaluated against that one read:

```text
  the resources the checks test (VMs, scale sets, disks, snapshots,
  storage, SQL, App Service, Key Vault, AKS, load balancers,
  Application Gateways, public IPs, NSGs, NICs, Cosmos DB, Redis,
  container registries, Recovery Services vaults, virtual networks,
  resource groups), VM extensions, autoscale settings, deployment
  slots, what Azure Backup protects, how many alert rules and action
  groups each subscription has, Azure Advisor's recommendations in
  the pillars' categories, and Defender for Cloud's plans, secure
  scores and high-severity assessments.
```

Each pillar is scored against its design principles (Microsoft
Learn):

```text
  Reliability  business requirements, resilience, recovery,
               operations, simplicity - zones, backups, redundancy,
               instance counts, retired Basic SKUs, health probes, SLA
               tiers
  Security     security readiness, confidentiality, integrity,
               availability, sustained posture - Defender plans and
               secure score, TLS, HTTPS, public access, network
               restrictions, keys and local accounts, management ports
               open to the internet, WAF, DDoS
  Cost         cost-management discipline, cost-efficiency, usage and
               rate optimization, monitoring - cost-allocation tags
               (-CostTag), unattached disks, unused public IPs, VMs
               stopped but billed, empty plans, old snapshots, Azure
               Hybrid Benefit, old VM generations
  Operational  DevOps culture, standards, observability, deployment,
  Excellence   automation - owner and environment tags (-OwnerTag),
               the Azure Monitor agent, boot diagnostics, Application
               Insights, alert rules and action groups, deployment
               slots, platform patching, AKS auto-upgrade
  Performance  targets, capacity, sustained performance, optimization
  Efficiency   - autoscale on plans, scale sets, AKS and Application
               Gateway, accelerated networking, SSD OS disks, SQL and
               Redis tiers
```

Advisor and Defender are checks too, one per pillar (AD-HA, AD-SEC,
AD-COST, AD-OPS, AD-PERF, DF-HIGH): a resource with an open
recommendation fails. An item that is the same finding as a catalogue
check on the same resource is counted once, by the catalogue check,
whose result says 'Also flagged by Advisor' (or Defender);
-KeepDuplicates counts both.

What no API can test - business requirements, threat models, budgets,
performance targets, team practices - comes from the questionnaire:
Export-AACWafQuestionnaire writes one question per principle, the team
answers Yes, Partly or No, and -AttestationPath scores the answers
(checks AT-..., heat-map column 'Attested'). -HistoryPath keeps a line
per run and shows the change since the last one.

Scores are out of 100: a check's is the share of resources that pass;
a principle's and a pillar's weigh their checks by severity (High 3,
Medium 2, Low 1). A principle no check covers is shown as not
assessed: it needs a review or attestation. Each pillar gets a
maturity: Initial (under 50), Developing, Established (75+),
Optimised (90+).

The heat maps - pillars, and design principles, by -HeatMapBy - show
each cell's score in colour: at the prompt (the first eight columns),
in the PDF (ten columns a table) and in the HTML report, where
clicking a cell lists its findings.

What you get depends on where the command runs:

```text
  at the prompt    tiles, the heat maps, the principles, and the top
                   findings - a page at a time
  piped onward     one AAC.WafCheckResult per check and resource
  -PassThru        the view and the results
  -NoDisplay       the results only
```

-CsvPath writes every result; -HtmlPath an interactive report
(summary with heat maps, principles, checks, findings); -PdfPath a PDF.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1

```powershell
Connect-AAC
Invoke-AACWafAssessment
```

All five pillars across every subscription, with heat maps by subscription.

### Example 2

```powershell
Export-AACWafQuestionnaire -Path .\waf-answers.csv
Invoke-AACWafAssessment -ResourceGroupName 'rg-app-prod' -AttestationPath .\waf-answers.csv -HistoryPath .\waf-history.csv -HtmlPath .\out\WAF.html
A workload's review with the team's answers, and its trend from run to run.
```

### Example 3

```powershell
Invoke-AACWafAssessment -ResourceGroupName 'rg-app-prod' -HeatMapBy ResourceType -HtmlPath .\out\WAF.html -PdfPath .\out\WAF.pdf
```

One workload's go-live review, as HTML and PDF reports.

### Example 4

```powershell
Invoke-AACWafAssessment -ManagementGroupId 'mg-landingzones' -Pillar Reliability -HeatMapBy ResourceGroup
```

The landing zones' reliability, resource group by resource group.

### Example 5

```powershell
Invoke-AACWafAssessment -NoDisplay | Where-Object { $_.Status -eq 'Fail' -and $_.Severity -eq 'High' } | Group-Object Check
```

The high-severity gaps, by check.

# New-AACServiceBlueprint

## SYNOPSIS

Plans the Azure services you name: what your tenant's Azure Policy allows, what PSRule for Azure says about a secure configuration, the alerts and resiliency guidance that go with them, the resources' names, and a diagram in draw.io, HTML or PDF.

## SYNTAX

### __AllParameterSets

```
New-AACServiceBlueprint [-Service] <string[]> [-SubscriptionId <string>]
 [-ManagementGroupId <string>] [-Region <string>] [-NamingConvention <string>] [-Workload <string>]
 [-Environment <string>] [-Instance <string>] [-Tag <IDictionary>] [-OutputFormat <string[]>]
 [-Path <string>] [-SkipPSRule] [-Title <string>] [-Force] [-Show] [-PassThru] [-NoDisplay]
 [-NoPaging] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm]
```

## ALIASES

This command has no aliases.

## DESCRIPTION

Name the services; nothing is deployed and nothing in Azure changes.
For each one the blueprint plans a secure starting configuration -
private, no shared keys or local authentication, TLS 1.2, a managed
identity, zone redundancy and soft delete where the service has them -
and checks it.

```text
  Naming      -NamingConvention filled in for each resource and checked
              against what Azure accepts for that type. A name that
              can't be used is reported, never shortened.
  Azure Policy  with -SubscriptionId: the policies in force for each
              type (Get-AACAssignedPolicy), the guardrails (allowed
              region and resource types, public network access) and
              Azure's own verdict on each planned resource
              (checkPolicyRestrictions). With -ManagementGroupId: what
              is assigned and the guardrails, no verdicts; Azure answers
              that question for a subscription. With neither: policy
              isn't read, no sign-in is needed, and the report says so.
  PSRule      PSRule for Azure's rules on each planned resource, as a
              deployment would present it. Rules about what a blueprint
              doesn't plan, such as an Event Hubs namespace's hubs, fail
              until you add it: they are a to-do list. The module's own
              naming rule is left out: -NamingConvention decides the
              names here. -SkipPSRule leaves PSRule out.

  Alerts      what Azure Monitor Baseline Alerts (AMBA) suggests for each
              type, as Get-AACAlertBaseline shows it.
  Resiliency  what the Azure Proactive Resiliency Library (APRL)
              recommends, as Get-AACResiliencyRecommendation shows it.
              Alerts and recommendations are suggestions, not results,
              so they don't change a resource's status.
```

Each resource is Blocked, Needs attention, Ready or Not fully checked.
Not checked is never reported as ready.

DeployIfNotExists and AuditIfNotExists policies look at other resources
after a deployment, so Azure gives no verdict on them beforehand. They
are listed on the Policies tab, not counted as passed or failed.

Services come from Azure's own list, the one behind the portal's New
support request page: tab completes them once you have run Connect-AAC,
and a resource type works too. That list says what a service's resource
types are, and nothing about how to configure one. So only FunctionApp
(with its plan), StorageAccount, EventHub and EventGrid, which have a
hand-checked secure configuration, get Azure Policy's verdict and PSRule.
Any other service is planned as its resource types, with the policies in
force, the guardrails, the alerts and the recommendations; it is never
better than Not fully checked, and its names aren't checked against
Azure's rules. Those four need no sign-in. A Function App needs a storage
account at run time: add StorageAccount, or you are told it is missing.

-OutputFormat writes to -Path. \<name\> is \<workload\>-\<env\>-blueprint:

```text
  DrawIo   <name>.drawio, editable, with a Legend page. An existing file
           isn't overwritten without -Force: it may hold your edits.
  Html     <name>.html, the diagram to pan, zoom and search, offline,
           and <name>-report.html, the tabbed report
  Pdf      <name>.pdf, the diagram (needs Microsoft Edge or Google
           Chrome), and <name>-report.pdf, the report
```

-Show opens what was written: the HTML page in your browser when there
is one, else the first file. Without -Path, the console view only.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1

```powershell
New-AACServiceBlueprint -Service FunctionApp, StorageAccount, EventHub, EventGrid -Workload orders -Environment prod -SkipPSRule
```

The names and the resources, offline: no sign-in, no policy.

### Example 2

```powershell
Connect-AAC
New-AACServiceBlueprint -Service FunctionApp, StorageAccount -SubscriptionId $sub -Workload orders -Environment prod -Tag @{ CostCenter = 'cc-123' } -OutputFormat DrawIo, Html -Path .\out -Show
```

Checked against the subscription's policy and PSRule; the diagram and report open in the browser.

### Example 3

```powershell
New-AACServiceBlueprint -Service EventHub -ManagementGroupId 'mg-landingzones' -NamingConvention '{workload}-{type}-{env}' -Workload orders -OutputFormat Pdf -Path .\out
```

What a landing zone assigns for Event Hubs, with your own naming pattern, as PDFs.

### Example 4

```powershell
Connect-AAC
New-AACServiceBlueprint -Service 'Virtual Network', 'Key Vault' -SubscriptionId $sub -Workload orders -OutputFormat Html -Path .\out
```

Services without a secure configuration here: the policies in force, the alerts and the recommendations for their types.

### Example 5

```powershell
New-AACServiceBlueprint -Service StorageAccount -SubscriptionId $sub -NoDisplay | Where-Object Status -EQ 'Blocked'
```

In a script: whether anything would be refused.

# Show-AACActivityLogEvent

## SYNOPSIS

Shows Activity Log events the way an admin reads them - when, what, the result and why it failed, who (decoded from the token), where - from the JSON the portal shows, a correlation ID, a Log Analytics workspace or the pipeline; as a console view, CSV, HTML and PDF.

## SYNTAX

### Query (Default)

```
Show-AACActivityLogEvent [-InputObject <Object[]>] [-CorrelationId <string[]>]
 [-SubscriptionId <string[]>] [-WorkspaceId <string>] [-Days <int>] [-Status <string[]>]
 [-ResolveIdentity] [-IncludeClaims] [-View <string>] [-CsvPath <string>] [-HtmlPath <string>]
 [-PdfPath <string>] [-Title <string>] [-PassThru] [-NoDisplay] [-NoPaging]
```

### Path

```
Show-AACActivityLogEvent -Path <string[]> [-SubscriptionId <string[]>] [-WorkspaceId <string>]
 [-Days <int>] [-Status <string[]>] [-ResolveIdentity] [-IncludeClaims] [-View <string>]
 [-CsvPath <string>] [-HtmlPath <string>] [-PdfPath <string>] [-Title <string>] [-PassThru]
 [-NoDisplay] [-NoPaging]
```

## ALIASES

This command has no aliases.

## DESCRIPTION

Read-only. An Activity Log event holds about sixty values, six levels
deep; the useful ones are hard to read as stored. Each event becomes
one flat row (AAC.ActivityLogEvent, ConvertTo-AACActivityLogEvent):

```text
  When    time, phase (begin or end request), ingestion delay
  What    operation, the authorised action and scope, category,
          channel, level
  Result  status, HTTP status and sub-status, and for a failure the
          innermost error code, message and target from the
          statusMessage (JSON inside a string), what kind of failure
          it is and what to do - as Get-AACResourceError reads it
  Who     user, guest, service principal, managed identity or Azure;
          app and object ID; how it signed in (public client, client
          secret, certificate or federated credential, or a user's
          authentication methods); home or external tenant;
          directory roles; when the token was issued and expires;
          caller IP. -ResolveIdentity names the service principal
          and the roles from Microsoft Graph
  Where   subscription, resource group, type, name, location, tags,
          a portal link
  Trace   correlation, operation and event IDs, tenant, hierarchy
```

The token's opaque values (aio, rh, uti, xms_\*) are left out:
-IncludeClaims adds every claim (Claim:\<name\> columns, and a Claims
view).

Where the events come from:

```text
  -Path            a JSON file: one event as the portal's JSON tab
                   shows it, an array of them, or a REST response
                   ({ value: [...] })
  -CorrelationId   every event of the operation, from the Activity
                   Log (90 days; -SubscriptionId, else every
                   subscription you can see) or, with -WorkspaceId,
                   the Log Analytics workspace it is sent to (as far
                   back as -Days and its retention)
  the pipeline     event objects or JSON text (ConvertFrom-Json,
                   Get-Content -Raw), or rows with a CorrelationId -
                   Invoke-AACActivityLogAssessment -View Activity and
                   Get-AACResourceError rows, for instance
```

Signed in, the events are enriched with subscription names and the
resource's location and tags; a file needs no sign-in.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1

```powershell
Show-AACActivityLogEvent -Path .\event.json
```

An event copied from the portal's JSON tab, readable: who, what, the error and what to do.

### Example 2

```powershell
Connect-AAC
Show-AACActivityLogEvent -CorrelationId $correlationId -SubscriptionId $sub -PdfPath .\incident.pdf
```

Every event of one operation, as a PDF to attach to the incident.

### Example 3

```powershell
Invoke-AACActivityLogAssessment -SubscriptionId $sub -View Activity -NoDisplay | Where-Object Status -EQ 'Failed' | Show-AACActivityLogEvent -HtmlPath .\failures.html
```

The full events behind the failed operations an assessment found.

### Example 4

```powershell
Show-AACActivityLogEvent -CorrelationId $correlationId -WorkspaceId $workspaceId -Days 365 -ResolveIdentity -IncludeClaims -CsvPath .\event.csv
```

From the workspace the Activity Log is sent to, with names from Microsoft Graph and every claim.

### -Days

```yaml

SupportsWildcards: false
Aliases: []
ParameterSets:
- Name: (All)
  Position: Named
  IsRequired: false
  ValueFromPipeline: false
```

# Show-AACApplicationGatewayMap

## SYNOPSIS

Draws Application Gateways as their connection flow - frontend IPs, listeners, rules, path rules and redirects, backend settings and probes, pools and targets, WAF policies - inside their network and subnet, with health and findings; shows each gateway's flows at the prompt and opens the map in your browser.

## SYNTAX

### __AllParameterSets

```
Show-AACApplicationGatewayMap [[-SubscriptionId] <string[]>] [[-ResourceGroupName] <string[]>]
 [[-Name] <string[]>] [[-CertificateDays] <int>] [[-Direction] <string>] [[-Theme] <string>]
 [[-HtmlPath] <string>] [[-CsvPath] <string>] [[-PdfPath] <string>] [[-Title] <string>]
 [-IncludeHealth] [-NoBrowser] [-PassThru]
```

## ALIASES

This command has no aliases.

## DESCRIPTION

Read-only, with Azure Resource Graph (Reader is enough): every setting
of each gateway, and what it refers to - public IPs, WAF policies,
the network and subnet (with its NSG and route table), the NICs and
VMs in the pools, and App Services whose host name is a target.

The map, left to right: frontend IPs \> listeners (protocol, port,
host names, certificate and its expiry, WAF policy) \> rules
(priority, basic or path-based) \> path rules and redirects \> backend
settings (protocol, port, timeout, host name, affinity, draining) and
their probes \> pools \> targets. WAF policies sit on the left with a
line to what they protect (the gateway, a site or a path). Pools and
targets are outlined green, amber or red by health. Click a card for
all its settings, its findings and its connections.

Health: metrics always (healthy and unhealthy host counts per pool,
last 30 minutes, v2 gateways); -IncludeHealth runs each gateway's live
backend health check - every target's state and, when it fails, the
probe's reason. That check takes 30-90 seconds and needs the
Microsoft.Network/applicationGateways/backendhealth/action permission;
a gateway that refuses is reported, not fatal.

Findings (High, Medium, Low): v1 SKU, WAF tier without a WAF, WAF in
Detection or disabled, old rule sets, old TLS policy, no zones or
under 2 instances, HTTP not redirected to HTTPS, certificates
expired, expiring (-CertificateDays) or uploaded instead of from Key
Vault, backend settings without a custom probe, probe host mismatch,
connection draining off, empty or unhealthy pools, and listeners,
settings, probes and pools nothing uses.

At the prompt: tiles, each gateway's flows (listener \> rule \> path \>
settings \> pool, with health) and the findings. -CsvPath writes the
flows; -PdfPath the gateways, flows and findings; -HtmlPath the map
(a file in your temp folder by default).

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1

```powershell
Connect-AAC
Show-AACApplicationGatewayMap
```

Every Application Gateway you can see, as a map in the browser.

### Example 2

```powershell
Show-AACApplicationGatewayMap -ResourceGroupName 'rg-edge' -Name 'appgw-prod' -IncludeHealth
```

One gateway with live backend health and the probes' reasons.

### Example 3

```powershell
(Show-AACApplicationGatewayMap -NoBrowser -PassThru).Flows | Where-Object Health -In 'unhealthy', 'degraded'
```

The routes that reach unhealthy backends.

# Show-AACCost

## SYNOPSIS

Shows what your Azure subscriptions cost - month to date and the last few months - as colourful Spectre.Console charts, with optional CSV, PDF and interactive HTML exports of the detail.

## SYNTAX

### __AllParameterSets

```
Show-AACCost [[-SubscriptionId] <string[]>] [[-Months] <int>] [[-Top] <int>] [[-CsvPath] <string>]
 [[-PdfPath] <string>] [[-HtmlPath] <string>] [[-Title] <string>] [-NoPaging] [-PassThru]
```

## ALIASES

This command has no aliases.

## DESCRIPTION

Asks the Azure Cost Management Query API, over REST with the
Connect-AAC sign-in (no Az modules), for each subscription's actual
cost over the last -Months months (this month so far included),
broken down by month, service and resource group - one query per
subscription, three at a time. The view:

```text
  ── Azure Admin Console :: Azure cost ──────────────────────────
  account · tenant · subscriptions · period · when
  [ month to date ] [ last month ] [ period total ] [ subscriptions ] [ top service ]

  Month to date by subscription   (when there is more than one)
  Month to date by service        (one bar split by service)
  Month to date by resource group (top 10)
  Last N months                   (one bar per month)
  Actual cost by subscription and month - with a total column and,
  for several subscriptions, a total row
```

Amounts are in each subscription's billing currency and never
converted; subscriptions billed in different currencies get charts
of their own. When Cost Management reports no cost at all for a
period, the view says so instead of drawing empty charts.

Subscriptions Cost Management can't report on (some offer types,
such as sponsorships, or missing permission) are listed with the
reason under the charts rather than failing the run. A subscription
with no cost in the period (new, empty, or billed elsewhere) is not
an error either: its Status is 'No cost', it is left out of the
charts and totals, and every output lists it as having no cost. Cost Management
allows only a few queries a minute, so a progress display shows each
subscription as it is read, and throttled requests are retried.

Exports:

```text
  -CsvPath    the detail: one row per subscription, month, resource
              group and service - SubscriptionName, SubscriptionId,
              Month, ResourceGroup, Service, Cost, Currency - ready
              for an Excel pivot table
  -PdfPath    a landscape A4 report: a summary (totals, the
              subscription-by-month table, top services and
              resource groups this month), then a page per
              subscription with its services and resource groups
              month by month
  -HtmlPath   a self-contained, interactive HTML report: tiles and
              charts (by month, subscription, service, resource
              group) that filter the detail, a subscription-by-month
              table and every detail row, with search, filters,
              grouping, totals of what is shown and a CSV download
  -PassThru   one AAC.SubscriptionCost object per subscription:
              MonthToDate, one property per month ('2026-07', ...),
              Total, TopServices and Status ('OK', 'No cost', or
              why the subscription couldn't be read)
```

When any of -CsvPath, -PdfPath or -HtmlPath is given, the console
shows only the progress and the files written - the report is in
the files. Otherwise the view is paged when it is longer than the
terminal: press any key for the next page, or A for the rest
(-NoPaging turns that off).

Reading costs needs Cost Management Reader (or Reader) on the
subscriptions. Costs are "actual cost" as Cost Management reports
it, which can lag usage by a day or so. PDF export needs Windows and
PowerShell 7.4 or later.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1

```powershell
Connect-AAC
Show-AACCost
```

Month to date and the last 6 months for every subscription you can see.

### Example 2

```powershell
Show-AACCost -Months 12 -CsvPath .\out\Cost.csv -PdfPath .\out\Cost.pdf
```

The last year as a detail CSV file and a PDF report.

### Example 3

```powershell
Show-AACCost -Months 12 -HtmlPath .\out\Cost.html
```

The last year in an interactive HTML report.

### Example 4

```powershell
Show-AACCost -SubscriptionId '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000' -Months 3
```

One subscription over the last three months.

### Example 5

```powershell
Show-AACCost -PassThru | Export-Csv .\CostSummary.csv -NoTypeInformation
```

One row per subscription, with a column per month.

## PARAMETERS

# Show-AACDashboard

## SYNOPSIS

A dashboard of your Azure estate: health, security, policy, governance, Advisor, the estate itself, the latest changes and (with -IncludeCost) the spend - one status and an Estate score at the top, and what to do next at the bottom.

## SYNTAX

### All (Default)

```
Show-AACDashboard [-Hours <int>] [-Section <string[]>] [-IncludeCost] [-HtmlPath <string>]
 [-PdfPath <string>] [-CsvPath <string>] [-Title <string>] [-Watch <int>] [-PassThru] [-NoDisplay]
 [-NoPaging]
```

### Subscription

```
Show-AACDashboard [-SubscriptionId <string[]>] [-Hours <int>] [-Section <string[]>] [-IncludeCost]
 [-HtmlPath <string>] [-PdfPath <string>] [-CsvPath <string>] [-Title <string>] [-Watch <int>]
 [-PassThru] [-NoDisplay] [-NoPaging]
```

### Select

```
Show-AACDashboard [-Select] [-Hours <int>] [-Section <string[]>] [-IncludeCost] [-HtmlPath <string>]
 [-PdfPath <string>] [-CsvPath <string>] [-Title <string>] [-Watch <int>] [-PassThru] [-NoDisplay]
 [-NoPaging]
```

## ALIASES

This command has no aliases.

## DESCRIPTION

Reads it all in one Azure Resource Graph batch (no Az modules), with
the Connect-AAC sign-in:

```text
  ── Azure Admin Console :: Dashboard ─────────────────────────────
  admin@contoso.com · tenant ... · all subscriptions · 9 Oct 2026 10:42
  ✗ Action needed  2 resource(s) unavailable; 1 active Azure service issue(s)

  [ subscriptions ] [ resources ] [ resource groups ] [ regions ]
  [ unhealthy ] [ Advisor High ] [ changes in 24h ]

  ╭─ Session ─────────────────╮ ╭─ Resource Health ──────────╮
  │ Account   admin@...       │ │ ✓ Available    1,204       │
  │ Tenant    ...             │ │ ✗ Unavailable  2           │
  │ Token     ✓ valid until … │ │ ⚠ Degraded     1           │
  ╰───────────────────────────╯ ╰────────────────────────────╯
  Subscriptions (state) · Resources by region · Azure Service
  Health - active events · Unhealthy resources · Azure Advisor
  recommendations · Recent changes (create, update, delete - what,
  where, who)
```

The status at the top:

```text
  ✗ Action needed     resources are unavailable, or an Azure
                      service issue is active in these subscriptions
  ⚠ Needs attention   resources are degraded, Advisor has
                      High-impact recommendations, planned
                      maintenance or an advisory is active, or
                      something couldn't be read
  ✓ Healthy           none of these
```

Beyond that one screen, from the same Resource Graph batch:

```text
  Scores       the Estate score (0-100: the average of the share of
               resources available, the secure score, the policy
               compliance and the Advisor score that could be read,
               less a little when a subscription nears the role
               assignment limit or spend jumps)
  Security     secure score, active alerts and unresolved
               recommendations by severity, Defender plans on
  Governance   policy compliance and the assignments with the most
               non-compliant resources, the closest role assignment
               limit, privileged role assignments at subscription or
               above, unused disks, public IPs and NICs, tag coverage
  Advisor      the Advisor score and the potential annual savings
  Estate       resources by type and by subscription
  Changes      the last 14 days, day by day, and who made the most
  Cost         with -IncludeCost (Cost Management, one query per
               subscription): month to date against the same days
               last month, a forecast, the last 30 days, the services
               that cost most
  Next         what to do, ranked across every section, with the
               command that goes deeper
```

-Section shows only some sections. -HtmlPath and -PdfPath write it
as a report - an Overview, then a tab per section; -CsvPath writes
what to do next. -Watch refreshes it every so many seconds, for a
screen on the wall (Ctrl+C stops it).

Symbols and colours are the module's (Unicode, or ASCII in a console
that isn't UTF-8), so the state never depends on colour alone. What
couldn't be read (Resource Health, Service Health, Advisor or the
change history need Reader on the subscriptions) is listed at the
end, and the rest is still shown.

Scope: every subscription the account can see, those in
-SubscriptionId, or - with -Select - those you tick in a list at the
console.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1

```powershell
Connect-AAC
Show-AACDashboard
```

The dashboard for every subscription you can see.

### Example 2

```powershell
Show-AACDashboard -Select -Hours 72
```

Pick the subscriptions from a list, with the changes of the last three days.

### Example 3

```powershell
Show-AACDashboard -IncludeCost -HtmlPath .\Dashboard.html
```

Everything, with the spend, as a report with a tab per section.

### Example 4

```powershell
Show-AACDashboard -Section Health, Security -Watch 300
```

Health and security, refreshed every five minutes.

### Example 5

```powershell
(Show-AACDashboard -NoDisplay).Actions | Format-Table
```

What to do next, as objects.

### Example 6

```powershell
(Show-AACDashboard -NoDisplay).UnhealthyResources | Format-Table
```

The unavailable and degraded resources, as objects.

### Example 7

```powershell
if ((Show-AACDashboard -SubscriptionId $prod -NoDisplay).Status -eq 'Failed') { Send-MyAlert }
```

Act on the dashboard's status in a script.

# Show-AACEffectivePolicy

## SYNOPSIS

Shows the Azure Policy that applies to a resource - one that exists, or one you are about to deploy - and what each policy does to it: blocks, audits, changes or deploys, where it is assigned, its compliance state and why, and what exempts or leaves it out.

## SYNTAX

### Resource (Default)

```
Show-AACEffectivePolicy -ResourceId <string[]> [-Impact <string[]>] [-IncludeNotApplicable]
 [-SkipReason] [-View <string>] [-CsvPath <string>] [-HtmlPath <string>] [-PdfPath <string>]
 [-Title <string>] [-PassThru] [-NoDisplay] [-NoPaging]
```

### Scope

```
Show-AACEffectivePolicy -SubscriptionId <string> [-ResourceGroupName <string[]>]
 [-ResourceType <string[]>] [-Impact <string[]>] [-IncludeNotApplicable] [-SkipReason]
 [-MaxResource <int>] [-View <string>] [-CsvPath <string>] [-HtmlPath <string>] [-PdfPath <string>]
 [-Title <string>] [-PassThru] [-NoDisplay] [-NoPaging]
```

### Planned

```
Show-AACEffectivePolicy -ResourceType <string[]> -Scope <string> [-Location <string>]
 [-Name <string>] [-Tag <hashtable>] [-Sku <string>] [-Kind <string>] [-Property <hashtable>]
 [-Impact <string[]>] [-IncludeNotApplicable] [-SkipReason] [-View <string>] [-CsvPath <string>]
 [-HtmlPath <string>] [-PdfPath <string>] [-Title <string>] [-PassThru] [-NoDisplay] [-NoPaging]
```

## ALIASES

This command has no aliases.

## DESCRIPTION

Read-only. Starts from the resource, not the assignment: every
assignment on its path - its management groups, subscription,
resource group and the resource itself - and, for an initiative,
each member policy, with one verdict:

```text
  Applies        the policy evaluates the resource
  Exempt         an exemption covers it (Waiver or Mitigated, all
                 policies or some, until when)
  Excluded       the assignment's notScopes leave it out
  Not selected   the assignment's resource selectors leave it out
  Not targeted   the rule is about other resource types (shown with
                 -IncludeNotApplicable)
```

For each policy that applies: the effect in force - parameters
resolved through the initiative and the assignment, then its
overrides - and what it means here (Impact): Blocks (deny), Blocks
delete (denyAction), Audits, Changes (modify, append), Deploys
(deployIfNotExists), Manual, Disabled, or Reports only when the
assignment isn't enforced. Also its non-compliance message, the
assignment's managed identity (for remediation), definition version,
regulatory controls, mode and parameters.

An existing resource: Azure's compliance state, when it was last
evaluated and - for a non-compliant one - why: the field, the value
the policy expects and the value it found (Policy Insights).

A planned resource (-Scope with -ResourceType): Azure Policy is
asked what it would do (checkPolicyRestrictions) - what would refuse
it, audit it or change it, and the values allowed: locations, SKUs,
types, required tags. DeployIfNotExists and AuditIfNotExists act
after a deployment, so they are listed as such.

Findings: non-compliant resources a deny will refuse at their next
deployment, remediation that can't run (no managed identity) or
hasn't, exemptions ending within 30 days or expired, policies with
no result yet.

Needs Reader on the resources and their scopes; assignments,
definitions and exemptions are read tenant-wide from Resource Graph,
so those inherited from management groups you can read are included.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1

```powershell
Connect-AAC
Show-AACEffectivePolicy -ResourceId $storageId
```

Every policy that applies to one storage account: what blocks, audits or changes it, where it is assigned, whether it complies and why not.

### Example 2

```powershell
Show-AACEffectivePolicy -SubscriptionId $sub -ResourceGroupName 'rg-orders' -HtmlPath .\orders-policy.html
A resource group's resources, with a tabbed report: in force, non-compliant, exemptions, left out, the assignment chain.
```

### Example 3

```powershell
Show-AACEffectivePolicy -Scope "/subscriptions/$sub/resourceGroups/rg-new" -ResourceType 'Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts' -Location 'westeurope' -Sku 'Standard_LRS' -Tag @{ CostCenter = 'cc-01' }
```

Before deploying: what Azure Policy would refuse, audit, change or deploy for a new storage account there, and the values it allows.

### Example 4

```powershell
Show-AACEffectivePolicy -ResourceId $vmId -Impact Blocks, 'Blocks delete' -NoDisplay
```

Only the policies that would refuse a change to the VM, or its deletion.

# Show-AACManagementGroupMap

## SYNOPSIS

Draws the management group hierarchy as an interactive map - the tenant root and management groups as nested boxes, each subscription inside its group - with the subscriptions, policy assignments and role assignments at each level.

## SYNTAX

### __AllParameterSets

```
Show-AACManagementGroupMap [[-ManagementGroupId] <string[]>] [[-SubscriptionId] <string[]>]
 [[-Direction] <string>] [[-Theme] <string>] [[-HtmlPath] <string>] [[-Title] <string>] [-NoBrowser]
 [-PassThru]
```

## ALIASES

This command has no aliases.

## DESCRIPTION

Reads, read-only and tenant-wide in Azure Resource Graph, the
management groups and their parents, the subscriptions, the policy
and role assignments per scope and the resources per subscription,
and writes the map as one self-contained HTML page (the same page as
Show-AACResourceMap: pan, zoom, search, click for details, save PNG,
JPEG, SVG or draw.io). At the prompt: the hierarchy as a tree with
the counts.

Unscoped, every management group appears, empty ones too; with
-ManagementGroupId or -SubscriptionId, only the subscriptions in
scope and the groups above them. For an editable diagram, use
Export-AACDiagram -View Governance. Reader is enough.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1

```powershell
Show-AACManagementGroupMap
```

The whole hierarchy, opened in the browser.

### Example 2

```powershell
Show-AACManagementGroupMap -ManagementGroupId 'mg-landingzones' -Theme Light -HtmlPath .\Hierarchy.html -NoBrowser
```

The landing zones' part of the hierarchy, written to a file.

### Example 3

```powershell
Show-AACManagementGroupMap -NoBrowser -PassThru | Sort-Object PolicyAssignments -Descending | Select-Object -First 5
```

The management groups with the most policy assignments.
