# Show-AACNetworkTopology

## SYNOPSIS

Draws the network topology of the tenant - or of management groups, subscriptions or regions - as an interactive diagram: hubs with their spokes around them, or every network inside its tenant, management group, subscription, region and resource group; with the peerings, private endpoints and the firewalls and appliances traffic is routed through. Opens it in your browser, ready to save as PNG, JPEG or SVG.

## SYNTAX

### __AllParameterSets

```
Show-AACNetworkTopology [[-ManagementGroupId] <string[]>] [[-SubscriptionId] <string[]>]
 [[-Location] <string[]>] [[-GroupBy] <string>] [[-Layout] <string>] [[-ExcludeType] <string[]>]
 [[-Direction] <string>] [[-Theme] <string>] [[-NsgView] <string>] [[-HtmlPath] <string>]
 [[-Title] <string>] [-NetworkOnly] [-NoBrowser] [-PassThru]
```

## ALIASES

This command has no aliases.

## DESCRIPTION

Reads with Azure Resource Graph - read-only, Reader is enough, no Az
modules - across every subscription in scope, every region:

```text
  the management groups and subscriptions above the networks
  virtual networks and subnets, and their peerings - also across
    subscriptions, and to networks you can't see
  VPN and ExpressRoute gateways, connections, circuits, local
    gateways; Virtual WAN and its hubs and gateways
  Azure Firewalls, network virtual appliances (VMs whose NIC forwards
    IP traffic), NSGs, route tables, NAT gateways, Bastion, load
    balancers, Application Gateways, private link services, DNS
    resolvers
  virtual machines, scale sets and private endpoints in their
    subnets, and the PaaS resources the private endpoints serve
    (-NetworkOnly leaves these out)
```

A peering outside the scope is followed to the network at its other
end, and a route's next hop to the firewall or appliance that has the
IP, so a spoke's map reaches its hub.

The boxes (-GroupBy):

```text
  ManagementGroup  tenant > management group > subscription > region
                   > resource group > virtual network > subnet
  Subscription     subscription > region > resource group > ...
  Region           region > virtual network > subnet
```

Subnets are drawn in rows inside their network, as wide as their
prefix is big. VMs, scale sets, Bastion, gateways, firewalls and
private endpoints sit in the subnet they have an IP in; a VM shows
its NIC's IPs and NSG, and an appliance is outlined in the route
colour.

The lines:

```text
  VNet peering   between networks, both ways, with its state and what
                 it lets through (forwarded traffic, gateway transit,
                 remote gateway); red and dashed when not Connected
  Private link   from a private endpoint to the PaaS resource it serves
  Route          from a subnet to the firewall or appliance its routes
                 send traffic to ("0.0.0.0/0 via rt-spoke")
  Network        a gateway's connections and circuits, and the rest
```

Within a network, subnets reach each other through Azure's system
routes: no lines are drawn between them.

Each network gets a role: hub (gateway transit, or a gateway,
firewall or appliance and peerings, or 3+ peerings), spoke (peered
with a hub), peered or standalone. The layout (-Layout):

```text
  HubSpoke   each hub at the centre, its spokes in rings around it,
             hubs side by side, the rest below; each network's box
             says its subscription, region and resource group
  Hierarchy  the nested boxes, laid out in layers
  Auto       HubSpoke when there are hubs with spokes (the default)
```

The page switches between them, and between left to right and top to
bottom; pan, zoom, search, click for details and connections, and
save as PNG, JPEG or SVG.

At the prompt: tiles, the hubs and their spokes, and findings - a
peering that isn't connected, a route to an IP nothing has, a spoke
subnet whose internet traffic isn't sent through a firewall or
appliance, a peering to a network you can't see, standalone networks.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1

```powershell
Connect-AAC
Show-AACNetworkTopology
```

Every network you can see, hubs at the centre of their spokes.

### Example 2

```powershell
Show-AACNetworkTopology -ManagementGroupId 'mg-landingzones' -GroupBy Subscription -Layout Hierarchy
A management group's networks inside their subscriptions, regions and resource groups.
```

### Example 3

```powershell
Show-AACNetworkTopology -NetworkOnly -Location 'uksouth', 'ukwest' -Theme Light -HtmlPath .\out\Network.html -NoBrowser
```

The network fabric of two regions, written to a file.

### Example 4

```powershell
(Show-AACNetworkTopology -NoBrowser -PassThru).Findings | Where-Object Severity -EQ 'High'
```

Peerings that aren't connected and routes to IPs nothing has.

# Show-AACResource

## SYNOPSIS

Shows how many Azure resources you have - by type, location, resource group or subscription - as a colourful Spectre.Console bar chart.

## SYNTAX

### __AllParameterSets

```
Show-AACResource [[-SubscriptionId] <string[]>] [[-By] <string>] [[-ResourceType] <string[]>]
 [[-Top] <int>] [[-HtmlPath] <string>] [[-Title] <string>] [-NoPaging] [-PassThru]
```

## ALIASES

This command has no aliases.

## DESCRIPTION

Counts every resource the signed-in account can see (or only those in
-SubscriptionId, of -ResourceType) with Azure Resource Graph, over
REST with the Connect-AAC sign-in - two queries however many
resources there are, and no Az modules.

The view:

```text
  ── Azure Admin Console :: Azure resources ─────────────────────
  account · tenant · scope · when
  [ resources ] [ types ] [ subscriptions ] [ resource groups ] [ locations ]

  Resources by type (top 20)
  compute/virtualmachines       ████████████████████████ 412
  network/networkinterfaces     ███████████████████ 398
  storage/storageaccounts       ██████████ 164
  ...
  37 other types                ████ 61
```

Each bar has its own colour. -By picks what is counted: resource
Type (the default), Location, ResourceGroup or Subscription. -Top
sets how many bars are drawn; the rest are summed in a final grey
bar.

When the view is longer than the terminal it is paged: press any key
for the next page, or A for the rest. -NoPaging turns that off.

With -PassThru the counts are also returned as AAC.ResourceCount
objects (Name, Count, Share), every one of them, not only the top.

-HtmlPath writes a self-contained, interactive inventory instead of
the view: every resource (name, type, resource group, location,
subscription, kind, SKU, tags) with Azure portal links, tiles and
charts by type, location, subscription and resource group that
filter it, search, filters, grouping and a CSV download. It needs one
more Resource Graph query, for the resources themselves. With
-HtmlPath the console shows only the progress and the file written.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1

```powershell
Connect-AAC
Show-AACResource
```

The top 20 resource types across every subscription you can see.

### Example 2

```powershell
Show-AACResource -By Location
```

How many resources are in each Azure region.

### Example 3

```powershell
Show-AACResource -ResourceType 'microsoft.network/*' -Top 10
```

The ten most common networking resource types.

### Example 4

```powershell
Show-AACResource -By Subscription -PassThru | Export-Csv .\ResourcesPerSubscription.csv -NoTypeInformation
```

Shows resources per subscription and saves the counts as a CSV file.

### Example 5

```powershell
Show-AACResource -HtmlPath .\out\Inventory.html
```

Every resource in an interactive HTML inventory, with portal links.

## PARAMETERS

### -By

What to count by: Type (default), Location, ResourceGroup or
Subscription.

```yaml

SupportsWildcards: false

  Position: 1
  IsRequired: false

  ValueFromRemainingArguments: false
DontShow: false
AcceptedValues: []
HelpMessage: ''
```

Write an interactive HTML inventory of the resources to this file

# Show-AACResourceMap

## SYNOPSIS

Draws a map of the resources in one or more resource groups - with their connections, dependencies and network paths - and opens it in your browser, ready to save as a PNG or JPEG image.

## SYNTAX

### __AllParameterSets

```
Show-AACResourceMap [[-SubscriptionId] <string[]>] [[-ResourceGroupName] <string[]>]
 [[-Direction] <string>] [[-Theme] <string>] [[-NsgView] <string>] [[-ExcludeType] <string[]>]
 [[-HtmlPath] <string>] [[-Title] <string>] [-NoBrowser] [-PassThru]
```

## ALIASES

This command has no aliases.

## DESCRIPTION

Reads the resources with Azure Resource Graph (Reader access is
enough; no Az modules) and draws them with their official Azure icons,
laid out by the Eclipse Layout Kernel (ELK), in boxes:

```text
  subscription > resource group > virtual network > subnet
```

A network interface, private endpoint, firewall, gateway, Bastion,
internal load balancer, AKS cluster or API Management service is drawn
in the subnet it has an IP in, and a virtual machine in the subnet of
its first network interface. Each resource shows its name, its
product, and a detail worth seeing: a VM's size, an IP address, a
disk's size.

The lines between them come from the resource IDs in each resource's
properties, typed by what they are:

```text
  Network association   NICs, IPs, subnets, NSGs, route tables, NAT,
                        gateways, VNet integration
  Resource dependency   an app on its plan, a VM on its disks, a
                        database on its server, a diagnostic target
  VNet peering          with its state
  Private link          a private endpoint to the resource it serves
  Route (next hop)      a route table to the firewall or appliance
                        its routes send traffic to
  Private DNS link      a private DNS zone linked to a network
```

NSGs and route tables are drawn the way a network engineer reads them:
as chips on the subnets and NICs they are applied to (-NsgView Cards
draws them as resources with lines instead). Click one for its rules
or routes. A chip is red when it opens a management or database port
(SSH, RDP, WinRM, SMB, SQL, ...) or every port to the internet, or
when a route's next hop is an IP no resource you can see has; amber
for a wide port range open to the internet, or 0.0.0.0/0 straight to
the internet. A subnet's routes are drawn from the subnet ("0.0.0.0/0
via rt-spoke") to the firewall or appliance they go through - looked
up across every subscription you can see, so a spoke's map reaches
the hub's firewall. Each subnet's box also shows how many of its
addresses are used and what it's delegated to, and each peering what
it lets through (forwarded traffic, gateway transit, remote gateway).

A resource outside the chosen resource groups that a chosen one uses
- a VNet in the hub's resource group, say - is drawn too, in its own
resource group's box, marked as outside the selection. Resources
attached to nothing (a network interface without a VM, a public IP
without a configuration, an unattached disk, an NSG or route table on
nothing) are flagged.

The map is one self-contained HTML file, written to -HtmlPath (a file
in your temp folder by default) and opened in your default browser.
In the browser you can:

```text
  - pan and zoom, and fit the map to the window
  - click a resource or box: its connections light up and the rest
    fades, with its details, connections and an Azure portal link
  - find a resource by name, type, IP or resource group
  - switch between left to right and top to bottom, and the Dark,
    Light and Blueprint themes
  - show or hide each kind of connection
  - save the map as a PNG or JPEG image (or SVG), as drawn
```

The Azure icons are Microsoft's Azure architecture icons, used under
Microsoft's terms for architecture diagrams (lib\azure-icons\SOURCES.md).

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1

```powershell
Connect-AAC
Show-AACResourceMap -SubscriptionId '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000' -ResourceGroupName 'rg-app'
```

One resource group's map, opened in the browser.

### Example 2

```powershell
Show-AACResourceMap -SubscriptionId $hub, $spoke -ResourceGroupName 'rg-hub', 'rg-spoke-app', 'rg-spoke-data' -Direction TopToBottom
A hub-and-spoke network across two subscriptions, top to bottom.
```

### Example 3

```powershell
Show-AACResourceMap -ResourceGroupName 'rg-app' -Theme Light -HtmlPath .\out\rg-app-map.html -NoBrowser
A light-themed map written to a file, not opened.
```

### Example 4

```powershell
(Show-AACResourceMap -ResourceGroupName 'rg-app' -NoBrowser -PassThru).Nodes | Where-Object Orphan
```

The resources attached to nothing.

# Show-AACServiceBusEntity

## SYNOPSIS

Shows Service Bus queues and topics as you can see them - live message counts, dead-letters, subscriptions, configuration and, with access to the namespace, their metrics - whether your role is on the namespace or only on the entities.

## SYNTAX

### __AllParameterSets

```
Show-AACServiceBusEntity [-NamespaceId] <string> [[-EntityName] <string[]>] [[-EntityKind] <string>]
 [[-TimeRange] <string>] [[-Sample] <int>] [[-SampleInterval] <timespan>] [[-View] <string>]
 [[-ThrottleLimit] <int>] [[-CsvPath] <string>] [[-HtmlPath] <string>] [[-PdfPath] <string>]
 [[-Title] <string>] [-SkipMetrics] [-PassThru] [-NoDisplay] [-NoPaging]
```

## ALIASES

This command has no aliases.

## DESCRIPTION

Read-only. Works out what your sign-in can read, entity by entity:

```text
  namespace role   Reader, Monitoring Reader or Data Owner on the
                   namespace: names can use wildcards (or be left out
                   to list every queue and topic), and each entity's
                   Azure Monitor metrics are read over -TimeRange
  entity role      Azure Service Bus Data Sender or Receiver on a
                   queue or topic: exact names only, live state only -
                   Service Bus publishes metrics on the namespace, so
                   an entity role can't read them. -Sample reads the
                   live counts a few times instead, for a short trend.
```

Live state (Resource Manager): active, dead-lettered, scheduled,
transfer and transfer dead-lettered messages, size against the
maximum, status, when last used, each topic subscription's counts,
and every setting (lock duration, max delivery count, TTL, sessions,
duplicate detection, forwarding, partitioning, auto-delete).

Metrics (namespace access): incoming, outgoing, completed and
abandoned messages, requests, server and user errors, throttling,
active, dead-lettered and scheduled messages over time, size, bytes,
send latency - per queue or topic (Azure has none per subscription) -
and a Premium namespace's CPU and memory.

Findings: dead-letters, transfer dead-letters, entities filling up
or not active, throttling, server errors, messages arriving with none
received, a growing backlog, entities unused for 30 days, expired
messages dropped - and entities you have no role on or that don't
exist.

-View sets what is returned (piped onward, -PassThru, -NoDisplay) and
written to -CsvPath: Entity (default), Subscription, Metric, Sample,
Finding or Access.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1

```powershell
Connect-AAC
Show-AACServiceBusEntity -NamespaceId $namespaceId -EntityName 'orders'
```

One queue or topic: its live state, and its metrics if you can read the namespace.

### Example 2

```powershell
Show-AACServiceBusEntity -NamespaceId $namespaceId -EntityName 'orders-*' -TimeRange 7d -HtmlPath .\sb.html
```

Every queue and topic starting orders-, with a week of metrics, as a tabbed report (namespace access).

### Example 3

```powershell
Show-AACServiceBusEntity -NamespaceId $namespaceId -EntityName 'orders' -Sample 10 -SampleInterval 00:00:30
```

With an entity role only: ten reads, 30 seconds apart, show whether the backlog is growing.

### Example 4

```powershell
Show-AACServiceBusEntity -NamespaceId $namespaceId -EntityName 'events' -View Subscription -NoDisplay | Where-Object DeadLettered
A topic's subscriptions with dead-lettered messages.
```

# Test-AACAlzPolicy

## SYNOPSIS

Compares the policy assignments on your management groups with the Azure Landing Zones reference - what each archetype assigns - and lists what is missing, assigned differently, or present.

## SYNTAX

### __AllParameterSets

```
Test-AACAlzPolicy [-LibraryPath] <string> [[-Architecture] <string>]
 [[-ManagementGroupMap] <hashtable>] [[-Status] <string[]>] [[-CsvPath] <string>]
 [[-HtmlPath] <string>] [[-PdfPath] <string>] [[-Title] <string>] [-PassThru] [-NoDisplay]
 [-NoPaging]
```

## ALIASES

This command has no aliases.

## DESCRIPTION

Reads a local copy of the Azure Landing Zones Library (clone
github.com/Azure/Azure-Landing-Zones-Library at the release you want
to compare with; nothing is downloaded): the architecture's
management groups (by default 'alz': the root, Platform,
Connectivity, Identity, Management, Landing zones, Corp, Online,
Sandbox, Decommissioned...), the archetypes each one gets and the
policy assignments each archetype makes. Then reads, read-only and
tenant-wide in Azure Resource Graph, the management groups and the
policy assignments deployed on them.

A row per assignment the reference makes on a management group
(AAC.AlzPolicyCheck):

```text
  Missing    nothing with that name or definition is assigned there
             (Medium) - the library file to deploy it from is named
  Different  assigned, with another definition (an older or newer
             version, or a replacement), or not enforced where the
             reference enforces (Low)
  Present    assigned as the reference has it
```

A reference management group that doesn't exist in the tenant is
one Info row: map the reference's IDs to yours with
-ManagementGroupMap. Reader on the management groups is enough.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/Azure/Azure-Landing-Zones-Library C:\alz-library
Test-AACAlzPolicy -LibraryPath C:\alz-library -ManagementGroupMap @{ alz = 'contoso' }
```

Your hierarchy against the reference, the intermediate root named 'contoso'.

### Example 2

```powershell
Test-AACAlzPolicy -LibraryPath C:\alz-library -Status Missing -NoDisplay | Select-Object ManagementGroup, Assignment, LibraryFile
```

What to deploy, and the library file to deploy it from.

# Test-AACAzureLimit

## SYNOPSIS

Shows which scopes are close to an Azure limit - role assignments, custom roles, policy assignments, definitions, initiatives and exemptions, resource groups, tags, management group depth - before a deployment fails on one.

## SYNTAX

### __AllParameterSets

```
Test-AACAzureLimit [[-SubscriptionId] <string[]>] [[-ManagementGroupId] <string[]>]
 [[-Status] <string[]>] [[-WarningPercent] <int>] [[-CriticalPercent] <int>]
 [[-Maximum] <hashtable>] [[-FailOnLimit] <string>] [[-CsvPath] <string>] [[-HtmlPath] <string>]
 [[-PdfPath] <string>] [[-Title] <string>] [-PassThru] [-NoDisplay] [-NoPaging]
```

## ALIASES

This command has no aliases.

## DESCRIPTION

Counts, read-only and in Azure Resource Graph (so only the totals
come back, however large the tenant), what each scope uses of each
limit:

```text
  Tenant             custom roles (5,000), custom initiatives
                     (2,500), management groups (10,000) and their
                     depth (6 levels below the root)
  Management group   role assignments (500), policy assignments
                     (200), custom policy definitions (500),
                     custom initiatives (200), exemptions (1,000)
  Subscription       role assignments at or below it (4,000),
                     policy assignments, definitions, initiatives
                     and exemptions, resource groups (980), tags on
                     the subscription and the most on any resource
                     group or resource (50)
  Resource group     policy assignments and exemptions - listed
                     only when they reach the warning level
```

Each (AAC.AzureLimit) has its use, the maximum, the percentage, what
is left and - when it is close - what to do. Critical at
-CriticalPercent (95%) or more, Warning at -WarningPercent (80%).

The maximums are Microsoft's published limits; if one changes, or
support raised one for you, pass -Maximum with the new number.
Reader on the scope is enough; management groups count when one of
the subscriptions in scope sits under them.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1

```powershell
Test-AACAzureLimit
```

Every limit in use across the tenant, the closest first.

### Example 2

```powershell
Test-AACAzureLimit -Status Critical, Warning -NoDisplay | Select-Object Limit, Scope, Used, Maximum, Percent
```

Only the limits that need attention, as objects.

### Example 3

```powershell
Test-AACAzureLimit -ManagementGroupId 'mg-landingzones' -FailOnLimit Warning
A pipeline gate: fails if anything under the landing zones is at 80% of a limit.
```

### Example 4

```powershell
Test-AACAzureLimit -Maximum @{ RoleAssignmentsPerSubscription = 6000 } -HtmlPath .\Limits.html
```

With a raised role assignment limit, as a report.

# Test-AACGoLiveReadiness

## SYNOPSIS

A go-live gate: runs the Well-Architected assessment on a workload and says Ready or Not ready - each pillar's score against a minimum, no high-severity findings, the checks that must pass - with the blockers, a Spectre.Console view, and CSV, PDF and HTML reports. -FailOnGap fails a pipeline stage when it isn't ready.

## SYNTAX

### __AllParameterSets

```
Test-AACGoLiveReadiness [[-SubscriptionId] <string[]>] [[-ManagementGroupId] <string[]>]
 [[-ResourceGroupName] <string[]>] [[-Pillar] <string[]>] [[-MinimumScore] <int>]
 [[-PillarMinimum] <hashtable>] [[-RequiredCheck] <string[]>] [[-AttestationPath] <string>]
 [[-HeatMapBy] <string>] [[-ExcludeCheck] <string[]>] [[-CsvPath] <string>] [[-HtmlPath] <string>]
 [[-PdfPath] <string>] [[-Title] <string>] [-AllowHighFinding] [-RequireAttestation] [-NoAdvisor]
 [-NoDefender] [-FailOnGap] [-PassThru] [-NoDisplay] [-NoPaging]
```

## ALIASES

This command has no aliases.

## DESCRIPTION

The same read and scores as Invoke-AACWafAssessment (one Resource
Graph batch, Advisor, Defender for Cloud, the questionnaire's answers
with -AttestationPath). Then the gates, each Pass, Fail or Warning:

```text
  Pillar score       each pillar at -MinimumScore (70) or more; a
                     pillar can have its own with -PillarMinimum
                     @{ Security = 80 }
  High findings      no failed high-severity catalogue check (Advisor
                     and Defender count through the pillar scores);
                     -AllowHighFinding turns this into a warning
  Required checks    every check matching -RequiredCheck (IDs,
                     wildcards) tested and passed everywhere
  Principles covered every design principle assessed, by a check or
                     the questionnaire; a warning unless
                     -RequireAttestation
```

Ready when no gate fails.

What you get:

```text
  at the prompt    the verdict, the gates and blockers, the heat maps
                   and the findings
  piped onward     the AAC.GoLiveReadiness object (Ready, Verdict,
                   Overall, Pillars, Gates, Blockers, Warnings)
  -PassThru        the view and the object
  -NoDisplay       the object only
```

-FailOnGap throws when not ready, after the view and any reports, so
`pwsh -File` exits non-zero. -CsvPath writes the gates; -HtmlPath and
-PdfPath the full report with a Go-live tab.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1

```powershell
Test-AACGoLiveReadiness -ResourceGroupName 'rg-app-prod'
```

Is the workload ready to go live, and if not, what blocks it.

### Example 2

```powershell
Test-AACGoLiveReadiness -ResourceGroupName 'rg-app-prod' -PillarMinimum @{ Security = 85 } -RequiredCheck 'RE-02', 'SE-1*' -AttestationPath .\waf-answers.csv -RequireAttestation -PdfPath .\GoLive.pdf
A strict gate with the team's answers, as a PDF for sign-off.
```

### Example 3

```powershell
Test-AACGoLiveReadiness -ResourceGroupName $env:WORKLOAD_RG -NoDisplay -FailOnGap -HtmlPath "$env:BUILD_ARTIFACTSTAGINGDIRECTORY/golive.html"
```

In a pipeline: the stage fails when the workload isn't ready, and the report is kept as an artifact.

# Test-AACPolicyDeployment

## SYNOPSIS

Tests an ARM template or Bicep file against Azure Policy before it is deployed: what policy would refuse, audit or change, resource by resource, why, and the values it allows - for a pull request or a pipeline gate.

## SYNTAX

### __AllParameterSets

```
Test-AACPolicyDeployment [-TemplatePath] <string> [[-ParameterPath] <string>]
 [[-Parameter] <hashtable>] [-SubscriptionId] <string> [[-ResourceGroupName] <string>]
 [[-Location] <string>] [[-FailOn] <string>] [[-View] <string>] [[-CsvPath] <string>]
 [[-HtmlPath] <string>] [[-PdfPath] <string>] [[-Title] <string>] [-PassThru] [-NoDisplay]
 [-NoPaging]
```

## ALIASES

This command has no aliases.

## DESCRIPTION

Read-only: nothing is deployed. The template's resources are worked
out offline (parameters, variables and most template functions;
Bicep modules followed - Get-AACTemplateResource) and each body is
sent to Azure Policy's checkPolicyRestrictions for the resource
group (or subscription) it goes to, with audits included:

```text
  Blocked      a deny would refuse it - the field, the expected and
               the found value, and the values allowed
  Audited      it deploys, but is reported non-compliant
  Changed      modify or append would change it as it deploys
  Passes       nothing refuses, audits or changes it
  Not checked  Azure couldn't be asked
```

Policies that act on what exists after the deployment
(deployIfNotExists, auditIfNotExists, denyAction) are listed as
After deployment, so "Passes" isn't read as "fully compliant".

What can't be known before deploying (uniqueString(), reference(),
a parameter with no value) is left out of the body, never guessed,
and named on the resource - a policy that reads it isn't judged.

A .bicep file is compiled with the Bicep CLI (bicep build) when it is
on the PATH. -FailOn Deny (or Audit) ends with an error when a
resource would be refused (or audited), after the report is
written - for a pipeline.

Needs Reader where the resources go. checkPolicyRestrictions honours
the policy and exemptions assigned at the subscription, resource
group and above.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1

```powershell
Connect-AAC
Test-AACPolicyDeployment -TemplatePath .\main.bicep -SubscriptionId $sub -ResourceGroupName 'rg-orders'
```

What Azure Policy would refuse, audit or change in the deployment, resource by resource.

### Example 2

```powershell
Test-AACPolicyDeployment -TemplatePath .\main.json -ParameterPath .\prod.parameters.json -SubscriptionId $sub -ResourceGroupName 'rg-orders' -FailOn Deny -HtmlPath .\policy-gate.html
A pipeline gate: a report for the run, and an error when policy would refuse a resource.
```

### Example 3

```powershell

```

For a resource group not created yet: the values policy allows for each resource's fields.

# Get-AACApplicationPermission

## SYNOPSIS

Lists every permission an enterprise application or managed identity holds - API permissions, delegated consents, Entra directory roles (and their scope), Azure roles, owned objects and groups - with findings for the privileged ones, as a Spectre.Console view, objects, and CSV, HTML and PDF reports.

## SYNTAX

### __AllParameterSets

```
Get-AACApplicationPermission [-Identity] <string[]> [[-View] <string>] [[-CsvPath] <string>]
 [[-HtmlPath] <string>] [[-PdfPath] <string>] [[-Title] <string>] [-SkipAzure] [-PassThru]
 [-NoDisplay] [-NoPaging]
```

## ALIASES

This command has no aliases.

## DESCRIPTION

Read-only. For each -Identity it finds the service principal - by
object ID, application (client) ID, app registration object ID,
display name, or an Azure resource ID of a user-assigned identity
(or of a resource with a system-assigned one) - and reads, with
Microsoft Graph and Azure Resource Graph:

```text
  Application permission    each API's app roles granted to it
                            (Microsoft Graph User.Read.All...) -
                            tenant-wide, no user signed in
  Delegated permission      scopes consented for all users, or for
                            one user
  Directory role            Entra roles: at tenant scope, on an
                            administrative unit (with what the unit
                            holds - New-AACApplicationPermission's
                            scoped roles show here) or on one object;
                            direct, or through a role-assignable group
  Directory role (eligible) the same through PIM
  Azure role                Azure RBAC, direct or through a group,
                            with the scope in words (-SkipAzure
                            leaves it out)
  Owner                     applications, service principals and
                            groups it owns
  Group membership          the groups it is in
  Requested (not granted)   API permissions its app registration
                            asks for without consent
```

Findings: privileged application permissions (Directory.ReadWrite.All,
RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory, AppRoleAssignment.ReadWrite.All,
Mail.Send, Sites.FullControl.All...); privileged directory roles at
tenant scope (Global Administrator, Privileged Role Administrator,
Application Administrator...), any other role at tenant scope;
Azure Owner and User Access Administrator, Contributor on a
subscription or above; privileged delegated scopes consented for
everyone; owning another application.

The Entra admin center shows these in different places - API
permissions only under the application's Permissions; directory
roles under Roles & admins (and the administrative unit); Azure
roles under each scope's Access control - this lists them together.

Needs the Connect-AAC sign-in with read access to the directory
(Directory Readers is enough). A part that can't be read is a
notice, not an error. PIM-eligible roles need a Microsoft Graph
token with RoleManagement.Read.Directory, which the client
Connect-AAC uses by default can't get: sign in with
Connect-AAC -ClientId \<your app registration\> (that delegated
permission, admin-consented) to include them; everything else is
listed either way.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1

```powershell
Get-AACApplicationPermission -Identity 'My-Enterprise-App'
```

Everything the enterprise application can do, and what is privileged.

### Example 2

```powershell
Get-AACApplicationPermission -Identity 11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555 -NoDisplay | Where-Object Kind -EQ 'Directory role'
```

By application (client) ID or object ID: its directory roles and their scope.

### Example 3

```powershell
Get-AACApplicationPermission -Identity '/subscriptions/<id>/resourceGroups/rg-app/providers/Microsoft.ManagedIdentity/userAssignedIdentities/id-app'
A user-assigned managed identity, by its Azure resource ID.
```

### Example 4

```powershell
'app-one', 'app-two', 'func-myapp-prod' | Get-AACApplicationPermission -HtmlPath .\AppPermissions.html -CsvPath .\AppPermissions.csv
```

Several at once, as reports.

# Get-AACEntraGroupMembership

## SYNOPSIS

Who is in your Entra ID groups - direct members and everyone in the groups nested in them - flattened to one row per group and member, with a Spectre.Console view, objects, and CSV, PDF and interactive HTML reports.

## SYNTAX

### __AllParameterSets

```
Get-AACEntraGroupMembership [[-GroupName] <string[]>] [[-GroupNameStartsWith] <string>]
 [[-CsvPath] <string>] [[-CsvLayout] <string>] [[-PdfPath] <string>] [[-HtmlPath] <string>]
 [[-Title] <string>] [-PassThru] [-NoDisplay] [-NoPaging]
```

## ALIASES

This command has no aliases.

## DESCRIPTION

Reads the groups and their members from Microsoft Graph, following
nested groups to the end (a loop is followed once):

```text
  -GroupName            these groups, by exact display name
  -GroupNameStartsWith  every group whose name starts with this
  neither               every group in the tenant
```

Both can be given together.

It uses the Connect-AAC sign-in - no second prompt: a Microsoft Graph
token is taken from it silently, as other APIs' tokens are. Your
account needs to be allowed to read groups in Entra ID, which members
of the tenant are by default. With an App Registration of your own
(Connect-AAC -ClientId), give it Microsoft Graph's delegated
Group.Read.All and User.Read.All permissions. Nothing is written to
Entra ID.

One row per member of each group (AAC.EntraGroupMember): GroupName,
GroupType (Microsoft 365, Security, Mail-enabled security,
Distribution - dynamic, role-assignable), GroupSource (Cloud, or
synced from on-premises AD), MembershipType (Assigned, Dynamic,
Dynamic (paused)), GroupCreated (UTC), GroupOwners ('Name (UPN);
...' - users and service principals - or '(No owners)'),
MemberName, MemberType (User, Group,
Device, Service principal, Contact), UserPrincipalName, Mail,
UserType (Member or Guest), AccountEnabled, JobTitle, Department,
Membership (Direct, Nested, or Empty for a group with no members),
Via (the nested path, 'Group \> Nested group'), Depth, GroupId and
MemberId. The same rows go to CSV, HTML and PDF.

What you get depends on where the command runs:

```text
  at the prompt    tiles and a table of the groups, then each
                   group in turn: its details (type, source,
                   membership type, created, owners, counts), its
                   direct members, and each nested group's members
                   under its path - a page at a time
  piped onward     the rows, with no view
  -PassThru        the view and the rows
  -NoDisplay       the rows only
```

-CsvPath writes the CSV - by default in Export-EntraGroupMemberShip.ps1's
layout: one row per group with GroupName, GroupSource (Cloud or
Windows Server AD), GroupType ('Security', 'Microsoft 365 / Dynamic',
'Mail-Enabled Security / Role-Assignable' ...), Members (everyone in
the group, flattened: direct members and the members of every nested
group at any depth - users, service principals, devices, contacts -
each once, or '(No members)') and NestedGroupMembers
(every nested group at any depth, by its path, with its own members:
'Group: a, b; Group \> Inner: c'), then Owners, CreatedDateTime (UTC)
and MembershipType. -CsvLayout Member writes the rows above instead, one per
group and member. -HtmlPath writes an interactive report: tiles, the
groups as a tree (each group's details, owners and direct members,
nested groups opening to their own members - searchable), charts,
and tabs with the groups, everyone in each group once (Direct,
Nested or both, and through which nested group) and every
membership row - filterable and downloadable as CSV. -PdfPath
writes a PDF: the summary, the groups, then a page per group with
its details, direct members and each nested group's members.
With any of them, the console shows only the progress and the files
written.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1

```powershell
Get-AACEntraGroupMembership -GroupName 'grp-finance', 'grp-hr'
```

Two groups, with everyone in them, direct or nested.

### Example 2

```powershell
Get-AACEntraGroupMembership -GroupNameStartsWith 'grp-azure-' -HtmlPath .\out\Groups.html -CsvPath .\out\Groups.csv
```

Every group whose name starts with 'grp-azure-', as an interactive HTML report and a CSV file - one row per group, as Export-EntraGroupMemberShip.ps1 writes it.

### Example 3

```powershell
Get-AACEntraGroupMembership -GroupNameStartsWith 'grp-' -CsvPath .\out\Members.csv -CsvLayout Member
```

One CSV row per group and member instead, nested members at every depth, with the path they came through.

### Example 4

```powershell
Get-AACEntraGroupMembership -GroupNameStartsWith 'grp-' -NoDisplay | Where-Object { $_.UserType -eq 'Guest' }
```

The guests in those groups, and through which group.

### Example 5

```powershell
Connect-AAC
Get-AACEntraGroupMembership -PdfPath .\out\Groups.pdf
```

Every group in the tenant you signed in to, as a PDF report.

# Invoke-AACM365Assessment

## SYNOPSIS

Microsoft 365 tenant discovery and security posture - Entra ID, Microsoft 365 and Intune - read from the Microsoft Graph REST API with one token, with zero-trust findings, as a Spectre.Console view, an object, CSV files and a tabbed, interactive HTML report.

## SYNTAX

### Assess (Default)

```
Invoke-AACM365Assessment [-Section <string[]>] [-StaleDays <int>] [-SignInDays <int>]
 [-CsvPath <string>] [-HtmlPath <string>] [-Title <string>] [-PassThru] [-NoDisplay] [-NoPaging]
```

### Permission

```
Invoke-AACM365Assessment -ListPermission [-Section <string[]>]
```

## ALIASES

This command has no aliases.

## DESCRIPTION

Read-only, Microsoft Graph REST only: no AzureAD, MSOnline,
AzureADPreview or Microsoft.Graph modules. Every call uses the one
Graph token of the Connect-AAC sign-in; about 25 calls run in
parallel, each followed through its pages.

-Section picks what is read (everything by default):

```text
  Entra         tenant details and directory sync, licences,
                security defaults, user and guest settings
                (authorization policy), cross-tenant access,
                Conditional Access policies and named locations,
                admin roles - active and eligible (PIM) - with each
                admin's MFA registration, every user's MFA
                registration, authentication methods, identity
                providers - and:
                  MFA coverage           registered and phishing-
                                         resistant MFA by members,
                                         admins and guests; the MFA
                                         policy's exclusions
                  emergency access       break-glass accounts (excluded
                                         from every policy, or by
                                         name): two, cloud-only,
                                         Global Admin, passkey
                  dangling admins        privileged roles held by
                                         deleted, disabled, guest,
                                         idle, synced accounts or apps
                  role overlap           Global Admin plus more, three
                                         or more roles, active and
                                         eligible at once
                  legacy authentication  actual IMAP, POP, SMTP AUTH,
                                         ActiveSync... sign-ins in
                                         the last -SignInDays
                  user consent           who can consent to apps, and
                                         the admin consent workflow
                  security defaults      off with no MFA, or on when
                                         Conditional Access is
                                         licensed
                  PIM role settings      MFA, approval, justification
                                         and maximum duration on
                                         activation; permanent
                                         assignments
                  groups                 who is in the groups excluded
                                         from Conditional Access and
                                         the groups holding roles
                  access reviews         of admin roles and guests
                  directory sync         password hash sync,
                                         accidental deletion
                                         prevention
  Threat protection (with Entra and Microsoft365) risky users and
                risk detections (Identity Protection), Microsoft
                Defender XDR incidents
  Applications  (with Entra) app registrations and enterprise
                apps: secrets and certificates expired, expiring or
                long-lived; over-privileged permissions (application
                permissions on Microsoft Graph and delegated
                consents, rated Critical, High, Medium); redirect
                URIs that are dangling (their host looked up in DNS),
                wildcard or not HTTPS
  Microsoft365  domains, Microsoft Secure Score and its controls
                (with the gap and how to fix each), SharePoint and
                OneDrive sharing settings, audit logging (Purview
                audit log search, from its Secure Score control, and
                the Entra audit log)
  Intune        tenant settings, enrollment restrictions,
                compliance policies, endpoint security policies
                (antivirus, firewall, disk encryption, EDR, attack
                surface reduction, account protection), managed
                devices (compliance, encryption, stale), the
                Entra ID devices no MDM manages, and app protection
                (MAM) for personal iOS and Android devices
  Microsoft365  (also) licensed users with no activity in 30 days
```

PERMISSIONS. A Graph token carries the permissions consented to the
app you sign in with. Connect-AAC's default (the Azure CLI) can read
the directory but not Conditional Access, Intune or Secure Score.
For everything in one token, sign in with an app that has the
delegated (or, for a service principal, application) permissions
-ListPermission prints - for example Microsoft Graph Command Line
Tools, once an admin has consented:

```text
    Connect-AAC -ClientId 14d82eec-204b-4c2f-b7e8-296a70dab67e `
        -Scope ((Invoke-AACM365Assessment -ListPermission) + 'offline_access', 'openid', 'profile')
```

Your account also needs a directory role that can read them (Global
Reader, Security Reader plus Intune Administrator or reader roles).
COVERAGE. The Coverage tab lists every lens - Assessed, Partly
assessed, Not assessed (with Graph's reason, the permission and any
licence it needs) or Not in this run - and what Microsoft Graph
doesn't reach at all (Exchange Online, Defender for Office 365,
Purview, Teams, Defender for Cloud Apps, Sentinel...), each with
what would cover it. The rest of the report is made whatever is
refused.

What you get depends on where the command runs:

```text
  at the prompt    tiles, the security settings, Conditional Access,
                   the privileged role assignments, what couldn't
                   be read and the findings, a page at a time
  piped onward     the AAC.M365Assessment object, with every table
                   as a property
  -PassThru        the view and the object
  -NoDisplay       the object only
```

-CsvPath (a folder) writes a CSV per table. -HtmlPath writes a
tabbed report - Overview, Findings, Entra ID, Microsoft 365,
Applications, Threat protection, Intune, Coverage - where every
table can be searched, filtered, grouped
and downloaded, and a row opens all its details.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1

```powershell
Connect-AAC -ClientId 14d82eec-204b-4c2f-b7e8-296a70dab67e -Scope ((Invoke-AACM365Assessment -ListPermission) + 'offline_access', 'openid', 'profile')
Invoke-AACM365Assessment -HtmlPath .\out\M365.html -CsvPath .\out\m365
```

Signs in once with every permission the report needs, then writes the HTML report and a CSV per table.

### Example 2

```powershell
Invoke-AACM365Assessment -Section Entra
```

Only Entra ID: settings, Conditional Access, admin roles and MFA registration.

### Example 3

```powershell
(Invoke-AACM365Assessment -NoDisplay -Section Entra).Registration | Where-Object { $_.Admin -eq 'Yes' -and $_.MfaRegistered -eq 'No' }
```

The administrators with no MFA method registered.

### Example 4

```powershell
(Invoke-AACM365Assessment -NoDisplay -Section Intune -StaleDays 30).ManagedDevices | Where-Object Stale -EQ 'Yes' | Export-Csv .\stale.csv
```

The Intune devices that haven't checked in for 30 days.

# New-AACApplicationPermission

## SYNOPSIS

Lets an enterprise application or managed identity manage specific Entra groups only - not every group in the tenant - with an administrative unit, a custom (or built-in) directory role and a role assignment scoped to the unit. Plan, confirm, apply, verify.

## SYNTAX

### Access (Default)

```
New-AACApplicationPermission -ServicePrincipal <string> -Group <string[]> [-Access <string>]
 [-RoleName <string>] [-AdministrativeUnitName <string>] [-RestrictedManagement]
 [-RemoveTenantWidePermission] [-Force] [-PassThru] [-NoDisplay] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm]
```

### Custom

```
New-AACApplicationPermission -ServicePrincipal <string> -Group <string[]>
 -AllowedResourceAction <string[]> [-RoleName <string>] [-AdministrativeUnitName <string>]
 [-RestrictedManagement] [-RemoveTenantWidePermission] [-Force] [-PassThru] [-NoDisplay] [-WhatIf]
 [-Confirm]
```

## ALIASES

This command has no aliases.

## DESCRIPTION

Microsoft Graph application permissions are tenant-wide:
GroupMember.ReadWrite.All lets an application add and remove
members in every group, and there is no "selected groups" version
of it (as Sites.Selected is for SharePoint). The same rights, over
chosen groups only:

```text
  1. Administrative unit   holds exactly the groups
                           (-AdministrativeUnitName; created when
                           missing, -RestrictedManagement on creation)
  2. Directory role        only the group actions (-Access, or your
                           own -AllowedResourceAction); a custom role
                           (-RoleName) is created, or updated when its
                           actions differ; a built-in role is used as
                           it is
  3. Role assignment       the role to the application, scoped to the
                           administrative unit - not '/'
```

The application's code doesn't change: it still asks for a
https://graph.microsoft.com/.default token and calls
POST /groups/{id}/members/$ref. Any other group answers 403.

Like Deploy-AACStorageAccount, it plans first - what exists is read
and only what is missing is written - and shows the plan. Findings
say what would undo the scope: a tenant-wide Graph permission
(GroupMember.ReadWrite.All, Group.ReadWrite.All,
Directory.ReadWrite.All - removed with -RemoveTenantWidePermission),
the same role at tenant scope, other objects in the unit, dynamic or
role-assignable groups. You are asked before anything is written
(-Force, or -Confirm:$false, for pipelines); -WhatIf stops after the
plan. After the apply everything is read again: running the same
command again plans no changes.

Needs the Connect-AAC sign-in with Privileged Role Administrator
(or Global Administrator) - a service principal needs the Graph
permissions RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory,
AdministrativeUnit.ReadWrite.All, Application.Read.All and
Group.Read.All, and AppRoleAssignment.ReadWrite.All for
-RemoveTenantWidePermission. Custom roles and administrative units
need Microsoft Entra ID P1. An application may cache its token for
up to an hour (a managed identity up to 24 hours) before the change
takes effect.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1

```powershell
New-AACApplicationPermission -ServicePrincipal 'My-Enterprise-App' -Group 'SG-Group-One', 'SG-Group-Two' -WhatIf
```

The plan: what would be created, and what would undo the scope.

### Example 2

```powershell
New-AACApplicationPermission -ServicePrincipal 'func-myapp-prod' -Group 'SG-Group-One' -RemoveTenantWidePermission
A managed identity (its Function App's name) gets member read/write on one group, and loses GroupMember.ReadWrite.All.
```

### Example 3

```powershell
New-AACApplicationPermission -ServicePrincipal 11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555 -Group 'SG-Group-One' -AllowedResourceAction 'microsoft.directory/groups/standard/read', 'microsoft.directory/groups/members/read' -RoleName 'Group Member Reader (Scoped)'
A custom role of your own, for an application found by its ID.
```

### Example 4

```powershell
New-AACApplicationPermission -ServicePrincipal 'My-Enterprise-App' -Group 'SG-Group-One' -RoleName 'Groups Administrator' -Force -NoDisplay
A built-in role, scoped to the unit, in a pipeline.
```

```text
  MemberRead               read the groups and their members
  MemberAndOwnerReadWrite  members and owners
```

# Invoke-AACADOAssessment

## SYNOPSIS

Assesses one or more Azure DevOps organizations - projects, pipelines (YAML, or classic with no YAML file - flagged) with their last run and delivery metrics, every task and tool they use (with versions), repositories, service connections, variable groups and environments with their security posture, the software bill of materials (SBOM) each pipeline produces, DORA and the move to GitHub - as a Spectre.Console view, objects, and CSV, HTML and PDF reports.

## SYNTAX

### __AllParameterSets

```
Invoke-AACADOAssessment [[-Organization] <string[]>] [[-Project] <string[]>] [[-PipelineId] <int[]>]
 [[-PersonalAccessToken] <securestring>] [[-Skip] <string[]>] [[-MetricDays] <int>]
 [[-TemplateDepth] <int>] [[-StaleDays] <int>] [[-InactiveDays] <int>] [[-StaleBranchDays] <int>]
 [[-ToolRule] <Object[]>] [[-ToolRulePath] <string>] [[-MaxScriptFiles] <int>]
 [[-YamlPath] <string>] [[-View] <string>] [[-ThrottleLimit] <int>] [[-CsvPath] <string>]
 [[-HtmlPath] <string>] [[-PdfPath] <string>] [[-Title] <string>] [-DiscoverOrganization]
 [-UseAzureSignIn] [-SkipYaml] [-IncludeAzure] [-IncludeDisabledRepository] [-PassThru] [-NoDisplay]
 [-NoPaging]
```

## ALIASES

This command has no aliases.

## DESCRIPTION

Read-only, through the Azure DevOps REST API - nothing is changed.
For each organization (-Organization, or -DiscoverOrganization) and
project (or -Project), it reads:

```text
  pipelines     every build pipeline: YAML or classic (designer,
                no YAML file), its folder, repository, state and
                last run, and every classic release pipeline
  steps         YAML pipelines' files from their default branch
                (Azure Repos Git) and the templates they include -
                local or template@repository, nested to
                -TemplateDepth; the script files, package.json
                scripts and Makefile targets they run (from the
                pipeline's repository); classic pipelines' tasks,
                named through the organization's task catalogue
  repositories  the last push, the branch policies on the default
                branch, GitHub Advanced Security for Azure DevOps
                (on or off, and active alerts by type and severity)
  security      service connections, variable groups and
                environments: who may use them, their checks
  runs          the runs of the last -MetricDays and each
                environment's deployments
```

Tools: one catalogue (about 150 tools) is matched against every file
a pipeline runs - its YAML and templates, script files, package.json
scripts, Makefile targets, a classic pipeline's tasks - and against
container images (fluxcd/flux-cli...). Categories: Lint, Build,
Test, Security, Deploy, Publish, GitOps (Flux, Argo CD,
Kustomize...) and Tooling (az, git, jq...). Every match is evidence
(-View Evidence): the pipeline, the tool, its version (an installer
task, an image tag), how it was found, the file and line, and the
line itself (credentials masked). -View Tool is the matrix of tools
with their pipelines, projects and versions; -View Coverage which
stages each pipeline has; -View Unrecognised the commands scripts
run that no rule knows (most-run first) and the templates and files
that couldn't be read. -ToolRule and -ToolRulePath add tools of
your own.

Tasks (-View Task): every task with its major version and what it
does (the task catalogue's description), packages installed at a
version, shells, container images, agent images and pools.

Findings: classic pipelines; never run, not run in -StaleDays, last
run failed, disabled; no security scanning, no tests, no linting;
deprecated or older task versions; unpinned container images;
retired hosted images; a value that looks like a secret written in
the YAML (its key and line - never the value); unreliable pipelines
and long queues; service connections open to every pipeline, using a
client secret rather than workload identity federation, or unused;
variable groups with secrets outside Key Vault, secret-looking
values not marked secret, open to every pipeline; production
environments with no approval, environments with no checks or open
to every pipeline; default branches with no required reviewers or
build validation; Advanced Security off, exposed secrets, critical
and high alerts; idle repositories.

SBOM (software bill of materials): which build pipelines generate
one - the Microsoft SBOM Tool (sbom-tool generate, the Manifest
Generator task, GenerateSBOM=true in .NET projects), 1ES Pipeline
Templates, Syft, CycloneDX, Trivy or Docker - and which validate one
(sbom-tool validate); then, from each one's latest successful run,
the SBOM it published (the _manifest/spdx_2.2 or spdx_3.0
manifest.spdx.json, or any SPDX or CycloneDX JSON file in its
artifacts): format, the tool that made it, components and files,
completeness against the NTIA minimum elements (name, version,
supplier, package URL), licences by kind (permissive, weak or strong
copyleft, unknown), and every component with its version, ecosystem,
supplier and licence. Findings: pipelines that deploy or publish with
no SBOM, an SBOM generated but not published, incomplete SBOMs,
strong copyleft licences, SBOMs never validated. -Skip Sbom leaves
the artifacts unread (the generators are still found in the steps).

Delivery metrics over -MetricDays: each pipeline's runs, success
rate (cancelled runs left out), average duration and queue time,
runs a week; each environment's deployments, deployments a week,
and change failure rate (DORA).

Branching: every branch with its role (from its name - develop,
release/\*, hotfix/\*, feature/\*...), last commit, ahead and behind the
default branch, stale after -StaleBranchDays, and the policies on it;
each repository's strategy (GitFlow, trunk-based with release
branches, trunk-based / GitHub flow, feature branching, single
branch). Every branch policy, on or off, with its settings in words
and its GitHub equivalent (rulesets, CODEOWNERS).

DORA, per project and for the organization: deployment frequency,
lead time (run queued to deployed), change failure rate and time to
restore, from production environments and classic release stages
(every environment when a project has no production one), each
banded Elite, High, Medium or Low; overall is the weakest.

Moving to GitHub: variables by name (pipeline settings, YAML,
variable groups - secret or not, never values), Azure Artifacts feeds
and their packages (and whether GitHub Packages can hold them), test
plans, wikis, service hooks, open pull requests, Git LFS, agent pools
and agents, marketplace extensions and the tasks pipelines use from
them, Advanced Security settings per repository and project; a
summary per project with rough effort points and a map of where each
kind of thing lands on GitHub and the tool that moves it.

-IncludeAzure (with Connect-AAC) follows each Azure service
connection to its service principal and the Azure roles it holds,
and flags pipeline identities that are Owner (or can grant access),
or Contributor on a whole subscription.

Signing in, in this order:

```text
  -PersonalAccessToken   a PAT with read scopes: Build, Code,
                         Project and Team, Release, Service
                         Connections, Variable Groups, Environment,
                         Advanced Security, Packaging, Test
                         Management, Wiki, Agent Pools, Extensions
  AZURE_DEVOPS_EXT_PAT   the same, from the environment (the
                         variable the Azure DevOps CLI reads)
  -UseAzureSignIn        your Connect-AAC sign-in (Microsoft Entra
                         ID), for organizations connected to your
                         tenant - no PAT to create or rotate
```

The token is sent only to Azure DevOps and never written anywhere.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1

```powershell
$pat = Read-Host -Prompt 'Azure DevOps PAT' -AsSecureString
Invoke-AACADOAssessment -Organization contoso -PersonalAccessToken $pat
```

Every project, pipeline and repository of the organization, with its tools, security posture and findings.

### Example 2

```powershell
Invoke-AACADOAssessment -Organization contoso -PersonalAccessToken $pat -HtmlPath .\ADO.html -PdfPath .\ADO.pdf -CsvPath .\ADO.csv
```

The same as reports.

### Example 3

```powershell
Invoke-AACADOAssessment -Organization contoso -PersonalAccessToken $pat -View Task -NoDisplay | Where-Object Kind -EQ 'CLI' | Group-Object -Property Name, Version
```

Every command-line tool the pipelines run, and the versions they set.

### Example 4

```powershell
Invoke-AACADOAssessment -Organization contoso -PersonalAccessToken $pat -View ServiceConnection -NoDisplay | Where-Object OpenToAllPipelines
```

Service connections any pipeline can use.

### Example 5

```powershell
Connect-AAC
Invoke-AACADOAssessment -DiscoverOrganization -UseAzureSignIn -IncludeAzure -HtmlPath .\ADO.html
```

Every organization you belong to, with each Azure service connection's roles in Azure.

### Example 6

```powershell
Invoke-AACADOAssessment -Organization contoso -PersonalAccessToken $pat -View Migration -NoDisplay | Sort-Object -Property Effort -Descending
```

Projects by how much work the move to GitHub is.

### Example 7

```powershell
Invoke-AACADOAssessment -Organization contoso -PersonalAccessToken $pat -View SbomComponent -NoDisplay | Where-Object { $_.Component -eq 'log4j-core' -and $_.Version -like '2.1*' }
```

Every pipeline whose latest SBOM ships a given component and version - the first question when a new vulnerability is announced.

### Example 8

```powershell
Invoke-AACADOAssessment -Organization contoso -Project Payments -PersonalAccessToken $pat -YamlPath .\pipelines -Skip Security, Metrics
```

Save the project's pipelines and templates to a folder, to review or diff offline.

# Export-AACArchitectureDecision

## SYNOPSIS

Step 6: writes architecture decision records (Markdown) for the design - topology, each pattern, each accepted risk.

## SYNTAX

### __AllParameterSets

```
Export-AACArchitectureDecision [-Design] <Object> [-Path] <string> [[-Accept] <string[]>]
 [[-Reason] <string>] [[-Owner] <string>] [[-ReviewBy] <datetime>] [[-GuardrailPath] <string>]
```

## ALIASES

This command has no aliases.

## DESCRIPTION

One numbered file per decision, plus README.md listing them with the
open decisions and assumptions. Files of the same name are
replaced. Offline.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1

```powershell
Export-AACArchitectureDecision -Design $design -Path .\adr -Owner 'Platform team'
```

The records and README.md.

### Example 2

```powershell
Export-AACArchitectureDecision -Design $design -Path .\adr -Accept 'REL-MR-01' -Reason 'One region for phase 1'
```

Also records an accepted risk.

# Get-AACArchitecturePattern

## SYNOPSIS

Step 2 (optional): shows which cloud design patterns fit the brief, why, and their Well-Architected trade-offs.

## SYNTAX

### __AllParameterSets

```
Get-AACArchitecturePattern [-Brief] <Object> [[-Top] <int>] [[-CsvPath] <string>]
 [[-HtmlPath] <string>] [[-PdfPath] <string>] [[-Title] <string>] [-RecommendedOnly] [-PassThru]
 [-NoDisplay] [-NoPaging]
```

## ALIASES

This command has no aliases.

## DESCRIPTION

Fifteen patterns from the Azure Architecture Center, best first.
Recommended means it fits the answers; New-AACArchitectureDesign uses
the recommended ones unless you pipe in others. Offline.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1

```powershell
Get-AACArchitecturePattern -Brief $brief
```

Every pattern, best first.

### Example 2

```powershell
Get-AACArchitecturePattern -Brief $brief -NoDisplay | Where-Object Id -In 'cache-aside', 'retry' | New-AACArchitectureDesign -Brief $brief -Offline
```

Design with the patterns you pick.

## PARAMETERS

### -Brief

The brief, or the path of a saved one.

```yaml
Type: System.Object
DefaultValue: None
SupportsWildcards: false
```

# New-AACArchitectureBrief

## SYNOPSIS

Step 1: captures a workload's requirements by asking about 20 probe questions, and returns the brief.

## SYNTAX

### __AllParameterSets

```
New-AACArchitectureBrief [[-Name] <string>] [[-Answer] <IDictionary>] [[-AnswerPath] <string>]
 [[-Level] <string>] [[-OutPath] <string>] [-NonInteractive] [-NoDisplay] [-NoPaging] [-WhatIf]
 [-Confirm]
```

## ALIASES

This command has no aliases.

## DESCRIPTION

At the prompt each question is asked in turn: Enter keeps the
default, ? means "don't know". Or give answers with -Answer or
-AnswerPath. Unanswered questions take their default (assumptions);
"don't know" answers stay open decisions. Offline.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1

```powershell
$brief = New-AACArchitectureBrief -Name 'orders-api' -OutPath .\orders-api.brief.json
```

Asks the questions and saves the answers.

### Example 2

```powershell
$brief = New-AACArchitectureBrief -Name 'orders-api' -Answer @{ 'BUS-01' = 'Web or API'; 'SEC-01' = 'Confidential' } -NonInteractive
```

Two answers given, the rest defaulted - no questions asked.

# New-AACArchitectureDesign

## SYNOPSIS

Step 3: builds the design - components, settings and connections - from a brief and the recommended (or chosen) patterns, and returns it.

## SYNTAX

### __AllParameterSets

```
New-AACArchitectureDesign [-Brief] <Object> [[-Pattern] <string[]>] [[-Region] <string[]>]
 [[-LandingZone] <string>] [[-Tag] <IDictionary>] [[-Override] <IDictionary>]
 [[-Commitment] <string>] [[-Name] <string>] [[-OutPath] <string>] [-Offline] [-NoDisplay]
 [-NoPaging] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm]
```

## ALIASES

This command has no aliases.

## DESCRIPTION

With no -Pattern, the recommended patterns are used. A landing zone
(-LandingZone, or the brief's answer) has its inherited policy and
allowed regions read from Azure - Connect-AAC first, or -Offline.
See the components with $design.Nodes.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1

```powershell
$design = New-AACArchitectureDesign -Brief $brief -Offline -OutPath .\orders-api.design.json
```

The design with the recommended patterns.

### Example 2

```powershell
$design = New-AACArchitectureDesign -Brief $brief -Region westeurope, northeurope -LandingZone 'mg-landingzones'
```

Two regions, checked against the landing zone's policy.

# New-AACArchitectureDiagram

## SYNOPSIS

Step 5: draws the design as Mermaid, Markdown and draw.io files, coloured by its findings, with compliance layers.

## SYNTAX

### __AllParameterSets

```
New-AACArchitectureDiagram [-Design] <Object> [-Path] <string> [[-Format] <string[]>]
 [[-Layer] <string[]>] [[-GuardrailPath] <string>] [[-Accept] <string[]>]
 [[-PSRuleBaseline] <string>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm]
```

## ALIASES

This command has no aliases.

## DESCRIPTION

Writes \<name\>.mmd, \<name\>.md (renders in Azure DevOps wikis, GitHub
and VS Code) and \<name\>.drawio into -Path. Green, amber and red show
each component's worst open finding; the layers add WAF badges,
policy, guardrail zones, the PSRule gate and Advisor. Offline.

The .drawio has five pages: Cover, Architecture (Azure icons in
landing zone, region, virtual network and data boxes, each layer
on a draw.io layer), Policy and compliance (inherited assignments
and the Azure Policy and PSRule rule for each component), Findings,
and Legend.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1

```powershell
New-AACArchitectureDiagram -Design $design -Path .\diagrams
```

All three files, every layer.

### -Accept

# Test-AACArchitectureDesign

## SYNOPSIS

Step 4: checks a design against the Well-Architected Framework, inherited Azure Policy, your guardrails and PSRule for Azure, and says what to fix.

## SYNTAX

### __AllParameterSets

```
Test-AACArchitectureDesign [-Design] <Object> [[-GuardrailPath] <string>]
 [[-Guardrail] <IDictionary>] [[-Accept] <string[]>] [[-CsvPath] <string>] [[-HtmlPath] <string>]
 [[-PdfPath] <string>] [[-Title] <string>] [-FailOnGap] [-PassThru] [-NoDisplay] [-NoPaging]
```

## ALIASES

This command has no aliases.

## DESCRIPTION

Each finding has a severity, pillar, the matching policy and PSRule
rule, and the fix. Blocking means Azure policy or your guardrails
would refuse the deployment. A guardrails file looks like
@{ AllowedRegions = @('westeurope'); DenyPublicEndpoint = $true;
DeniedSkus = @('Basic\*'); RequiredTags = @('Owner') }. Offline.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1

```powershell
Test-AACArchitectureDesign -Design $design
```

The findings and the score per pillar.

### Example 2

```powershell
Test-AACArchitectureDesign -Design $design -GuardrailPath .\guardrails.psd1 -HtmlPath .\validation.html
```

With your guardrails, as a tabbed HTML report.

### Example 3

```powershell
Test-AACArchitectureDesign -Design .\orders-api.design.json -Accept 'COST-RI-01' -NoDisplay -FailOnGap
```

In a pipeline: fails the stage while a Blocking or High finding is open.
